Options B, C and D are common causes of resistance, since people worry about their security, about uncertainty and about losing their position.

questions.question: A change agent is BEST defined as:

options.a: Anyone who resists new methods of work
options.b: A government official who registers companies
options.c: A worker who keeps existing procedures unchanged
options.d: A person or group who initiates, guides and supports change in an organisation

questions.explanation: A change agent takes responsibility for starting and steering change, for example by diagnosing problems, communicating the need for change and helping people adapt. Options A and C describe people who block or ignore change, and option B describes a regulatory role.

questions.question: Which of the following is a role of a change agent in organisational transformation?

options.c: Diagnosing problems and communicating the need for change

questions.explanation: A change agent studies the organisation to find what needs to change, explains why the change matters and supports people as it is implemented. Options A, B and D would weaken the change effort, because feedback, updated procedures and close contact with employees are all needed for change to succeed.

questions.question: A person who acts as a catalyst for change and takes responsibility for initiating and managing a change process in an organisation is called a:
questions.explanation: A change agent initiates, guides and manages change, and may be a manager inside the organisation or an outside consultant. Option B is a partner who takes no part in management, option A is Mintzberg's ceremonial role, and option D is an owner who may play no part in change at all.

questions.question: Which statement best describes a manager's responsibility for organisational transformation?

options.a: Managers should avoid change to protect stability
options.b: Managers should leave all change decisions to external consultants
options.c: Managers must recognise the need for change, plan and lead it, and help staff adjust to new ways of working
options.d: Managers need only announce change and staff will adapt automatically

questions.explanation: As change agents, managers identify when the organisation must change, set direction, plan implementation and support people through the transition. Option B shifts responsibility away from managers, option A confuses stability with standing still, and option D ignores resistance and the need for support.

questions.question: An EXTERNAL change agent, such as a management consultant, usually has which advantage over an internal change agent?

options.a: A more objective, fresh view of the organisation's problems
options.b: Lower risk of being seen as an outsider
options.d: Deeper knowledge of the organisation's history and culture

questions.explanation: An outside consultant is not tied to internal politics or habits, so he or she can see problems more objectively and bring new ideas. Options D and C are advantages of internal change agents, and option B is the opposite of the truth, since external agents are more likely to be seen as outsiders.

questions.question: A key DISADVANTAGE of an external change agent compared with an internal one is that the external agent:

options.a: Is too closely tied to internal politics
options.b: Has no professional training in change
options.c: May not fully understand the organisation's culture, history and people

questions.explanation: External agents often lack detailed knowledge of the organisation and may propose changes that do not fit its culture. Option A is a risk for internal agents, option D contradicts the usual strength of outsiders, and option B is not generally true of consultants.

questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes CHANGE LEADERSHIP from CHANGE MANAGEMENT?

options.a: Change leadership creates the vision and drives people to embrace change, while change management uses structured processes and tools to implement and control it
options.b: Change leadership is done by junior staff, while change management is done only by consultants
options.c: They mean exactly the same thing
options.d: Change leadership deals only with budgets, while change management deals only with vision

questions.explanation: Change leadership is about the 'why' and 'what': setting a vision, inspiring and energising people to move. Change management is about the 'how': plans, schedules, training and controls that keep the change on track. Option D reverses the emphasis, option C ignores the distinction, and option B wrongly assigns them by rank.

questions.question: The new CEO of a Nigerian bank travels to every region, paints an inspiring picture of a fully digital bank and urges staff to see themselves as innovators. This is mainly an example of:
questions.explanation: Creating and communicating an inspiring vision and energising people to move toward it is change leadership. Option D would involve detailed implementation plans, timelines and training schedules, option A is the final stage of Lewin's model, and option B means forcing people to accept change.

questions.question: A project office draws up a timetable for migrating 200 branches to new software, assigns responsibilities, schedules staff training and tracks progress against milestones. This is mainly an example of:
questions.explanation: Structured planning, scheduling, training and monitoring of a change are the tools of change management. Option C would focus on vision and inspiration, option B is the first stage of Lewin's model where readiness for change is created, and option D is a tactic for dealing with resistance.

questions.question: Which of the following is an EXTERNAL driver of organisational change?

options.c: The appointment of a new managing director
options.d: A new government regulation affecting the industry

questions.explanation: External drivers arise outside the organisation, such as regulation, technology, competition, economic conditions and social trends. Options C, A and B arise inside the organisation, so they are internal drivers.

questions.question: Which of the following is an INTERNAL driver of organisational change?

options.b: Entry of a new foreign competitor

questions.explanation: Internal drivers come from within, such as staff problems, new strategy, new leadership or poor performance. Options D, B and C all come from the external environment.

questions.question: A traditional bank finds that young customers are moving to mobile-only fintech apps, so it launches its own app and closes some branches. The main driver of this change is:

options.b: A change in the bank's ownership structure
options.c: Technological change and competition in the external environment
options.d: A decline in the population of Nigeria

questions.explanation: The pressure comes from outside: new technology and new competitors are changing customer behaviour, forcing the bank to adapt. Option A is internal and not described, option B is not mentioned, and option D is not true and is not the trigger in the scenario.

questions.question: Change that is deliberately designed and implemented in advance by management to achieve specific goals is called:
questions.explanation: Planned change is proactive and intentional, introduced after analysis to move the organisation toward desired goals. Options B and C describe change that happens in response to events or without design, and option A is not a standard type of change.

questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes INCREMENTAL change from TRANSFORMATIONAL change?

options.a: Incremental change is always unplanned, while transformational change is always planned
options.b: Incremental change makes small, continuous improvements, while transformational change fundamentally alters strategy, structure or culture
options.c: There is no difference between them
options.d: Incremental change affects the whole organisation at once, while transformational change affects one task

questions.explanation: Incremental change fine-tunes existing ways of working step by step, while transformational (radical) change reshapes the organisation as a whole. Option A confuses scale with planning, option D reverses the scope, and option C ignores the distinction.

questions.question: What is the correct order of the three stages in Kurt Lewin's change model?
questions.explanation: Lewin's model first unfreezes current behaviour by creating readiness for change, then moves to the new state, and finally refreezes the new behaviour so it becomes stable. Options D, B and C put the stages in an illogical order.

questions.question: In Lewin's change model, the UNFREEZING stage mainly involves:

options.a: Evaluating the change after it is complete
options.b: Making people aware that the current situation must change and preparing them for it
options.c: Installing the new system or structure
options.d: Making the new behaviour permanent through rewards and policies

questions.explanation: Unfreezing reduces attachment to old ways, often by showing evidence of problems, so that people become ready to change. Option D is refreezing, option C is the changing or moving stage, and option A is a later review step, not unfreezing.

questions.question: In Lewin's force field analysis, an organisation's current state is kept in balance by:

options.a: Only the forces pushing for change
options.c: The number of employees in the organisation
options.d: Driving forces pushing for change and restraining forces resisting it

questions.explanation: Force field analysis says the present situation is an equilibrium between driving forces and restraining forces; change occurs when driving forces are strengthened or restraining forces are reduced. Options A and B each consider only one side, and option C is irrelevant.

questions.question: A manager listing reasons for and against a new shift system writes 'competition from cheaper rivals' on one side and 'workers' fear of losing overtime pay' on the other. In force field terms, 'workers' fear of losing overtime pay' is a:
questions.explanation: A restraining force works against change; workers' fear of losing income makes them resist the new shift system. Option A would be the competitive pressure pushing for change, while options D and B are not terms used in force field analysis.

questions.question: In John Kotter's eight-step model of leading change, which step comes FIRST?

options.a: Anchoring new approaches in the culture

questions.explanation: Kotter argues change must begin by creating a sense of urgency so people see why the status quo cannot continue. Option A is the final step, while options C and D come in the middle of the model after a vision has been formed and communicated.

questions.question: In Kotter's eight-step model, the LAST step is:

options.a: Anchoring new approaches in the organisation's culture

questions.explanation: The final step makes the change stick by embedding it in the culture, norms and values. Option D is step two, option B is step three, and option C is step one.

questions.question: In Kotter's model, 'creating a guiding coalition' means:

options.a: Forming a union to oppose the change
options.b: Building a group with enough power, credibility and skill to lead the change effort
options.d: Asking the government to approve the change

questions.explanation: A guiding coalition is a team of influential people inside the organisation who work together to drive the change. Option C describes a merger, option D describes regulatory approval, and option A describes resistance rather than leadership of change.

questions.question: Three months into a new customer-service programme, a company publicly celebrates branches that have cut queue times by half to keep momentum going. In Kotter's model, this is:
questions.explanation: Visible early successes reward those involved and keep people committed, which Kotter calls generating short-term wins. Option C comes at the start before change begins, option B concerns forming the leadership team, and option D is a stage in Lewin's model, not Kotter's.

questions.question: Before introducing a new appraisal system, managers hold workshops, share data and answer questions so staff understand why the change is needed. Which method of reducing resistance is this?
questions.explanation: Education and communication reduce resistance that comes from lack of information or misunderstanding. Option D forces acceptance through threats, option A uses selective information or gives resisters a token role, and option C trades concessions for acceptance.

questions.question: A manager invites representatives of affected workers to help design a new work schedule, so that they feel ownership of it. This method of reducing resistance is:
questions.explanation: Involving those affected in designing the change builds commitment because people rarely resist what they helped create. Option A offers training or emotional support, option C relies on threats, and option D offers incentives in exchange for acceptance.

questions.question: To win the union's acceptance of a new automated line, management agrees to retrain affected workers and give a one-off bonus. This approach to resistance is:
questions.explanation: Offering something of value, such as retraining and a bonus, in exchange for acceptance is negotiation and agreement. Option C relies on information, option A relies on involving workers in design, and option B relies on covert influence or token roles.

questions.question: Management tells staff that anyone who refuses to use the new attendance system by Friday will lose their job. This approach to resistance is:
questions.explanation: Using threats of dismissal or other penalties to force acceptance is coercion; it is fast but can create resentment. Options D, C and A are supportive or persuasive approaches that do not rely on threats.

questions.question: Organisational development (OD) is best defined as:

options.a: A method of calculating the cost of production
options.b: The legal process of registering a new company
options.c: A planned, organisation-wide effort to improve effectiveness and health using behavioural science knowledge
options.d: A one-off decision to reduce staff numbers

questions.explanation: OD is a long-term, planned approach to change that applies behavioural science to improve how people and groups work. Option D is a single cost-cutting action, option B is incorporation, and option A is costing.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT usually a quality of an effective managerial change agent?

options.b: Communicating a clear vision of the change
options.c: Keeping plans secret from those affected until the last minute
options.d: Being willing to listen to concerns

questions.explanation: Effective change agents communicate openly, build trust and listen, because secrecy breeds fear and rumours that feed resistance. Options B, A and D are qualities that help change succeed.

questions.question: As a result of the 2004-2005 banking consolidation in Nigeria, the number of banks fell from about 89 to:
questions.explanation: Banks that could not meet the N25 billion capital requirement merged or were acquired, reducing the number of banks from 89 to 25. Options A, B and C do not reflect the outcome of the exercise.

questions.question: Under the bank recapitalisation programme announced by the CBN in March 2024, the new minimum capital for a commercial bank with an INTERNATIONAL licence is:
questions.explanation: The March 2024 circular set N500 billion for international commercial banks, N200 billion for national banks and N50 billion for regional banks, with a deadline of 31 March 2026. Option C is the national licence threshold, option D is the regional threshold, and option A is the 2004 consolidation figure.

questions.question: Under the CBN's 2024 bank recapitalisation programme, banks were required to meet the new capital thresholds by:
questions.explanation: The March 2024 circular gave banks 24 months to comply, so the deadline was 31 March 2026. Options B, D and C do not match the compliance window set by the CBN.

questions.question: When the CBN raised minimum bank capital in 2004 and again in 2024, bank managers had to raise fresh capital, merge or change their licence category. For those managers, the recapitalisation was mainly:

options.b: An internal driver arising from staff conflict
options.d: An external, regulatory driver of change

questions.explanation: The pressure came from a regulator outside the banks, so it was an external regulatory driver that forced major, often transformational change. Option B is internal and not the trigger, option C ignores that compliance was mandatory, and option A is the final stage of Lewin's model, not a driver.

questions.question: Nigeria's telecommunications revolution began when GSM licences were auctioned in January 2001. The regulator that conducted the auction was the:
questions.explanation: The NCC regulates telecommunications in Nigeria and conducted the January 2001 GSM licence auction. Option B regulates banks, option C registers companies and business names, and option A handles privatisation of public enterprises.

questions.question: At Nigeria's January 2001 GSM licence auction, each of the successful bidders paid a licence fee of:
questions.explanation: Each GSM licence cost 285 million US dollars. Option C was only the deposit included in that price, option B was the total raised from all three licences, and option A overstates the fee tenfold.

questions.question: Which two operators launched commercial GSM services in Nigeria in August 2001 after winning licences at the January 2001 auction?
questions.explanation: Econet Wireless began commercial operations on 7 August 2001 and MTN followed a day later. Globacom entered later through a 2002 process, so options B and D are wrong, and option A names brands that did not exist under those names in 2001.

questions.question: The Petroleum Industry Act (PIA), a major change in Nigeria's oil and gas sector, was signed into law in:
questions.explanation: President Muhammadu Buhari signed the PIA on 16 August 2021. Option D is when GSM licences were auctioned, option B is when the CBN announced bank recapitalisation, and option C is not linked to the Act.

questions.question: One major structural change made by the Petroleum Industry Act 2021 was that NNPC was to be:

options.a: Turned into a partnership of state governments
options.b: Converted into a cooperative society owned by its workers
options.c: Abolished and its assets sold to foreign oil firms
options.d: Incorporated as a limited liability company with the Corporate Affairs Commission

questions.explanation: The PIA required NNPC to be incorporated as a limited liability company with the CAC, with the Ministries of Finance and Petroleum as shareholders, so it would run on commercial lines. Options C, B and A do not describe what the Act provided.

questions.question: Under the Petroleum Industry Act 2021, upstream companies must contribute to host community development trusts an amount equal to what percentage of their actual annual operating expenditure of the preceding year?
questions.explanation: The PIA requires settlors to contribute 3% of their actual annual operating expenditure in upstream operations from the preceding year to host community trusts. Options B, A and D do not match the percentage in the Act.

questions.question: To regulate the oil and gas industry, the Petroleum Industry Act 2021 created:

options.a: A single regulator for banks and oil companies
options.b: Separate regulators for each of the 36 states
options.c: No regulator, leaving the industry fully self-regulated
options.d: Two regulators, one for upstream and one for midstream and downstream operations

questions.explanation: The Act created an upstream regulatory commission and a separate midstream and downstream regulatory authority. Options A, C and B do not describe the structure the Act set up.

questions.question: When GSM operators arrived in 2001, many Nigerian firms quickly changed how they sold goods, communicated with customers and managed staff in the field. For those firms, GSM was mainly a:

options.a: Internal driver of change caused by poor morale
options.b: Technological driver of change in the external environment

questions.explanation: Mobile telephony was a new technology arising outside the firms that forced them to change their processes, which makes it an external technological driver. Option A is internal and unrelated, option D confuses a driver of change with ownership forms, and option C is the last stage in Lewin's model.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a common reason why change efforts fail?

options.a: Failing to create a sense of urgency
options.b: Clear communication of the reasons for change
options.d: Not anchoring the change in the culture

questions.explanation: Clear communication helps change succeed, so it is not a reason for failure. Options A, C and D are classic causes of failed change efforts, each mirroring a step in Kotter's model that was skipped.

questions.question: A company that exists as a separate legal entity from its owners, able to own property, sue and be sued in its own name, demonstrates:
questions.explanation: Corporate personality means that once incorporated, a company is a legal person distinct from its shareholders. Option D is a feature of sole proprietorships and ordinary partnerships, and option C is the partnership rule that each partner can bind the others.

questions.question: Which of the following is a major weakness of a sole proprietorship?
questions.explanation: A sole proprietor usually depends on personal savings, family and small loans, so raising large capital is difficult. Options D and B are features associated with companies, not one-person businesses, and sole proprietorships actually face the lightest regulation of all ownership forms.

questions.question: Under section 305 of Nigeria's Companies and Allied Matters Act (CAMA) 2020, in force since 2020, a director stands in a fiduciary relationship primarily towards:
questions.explanation: CAMA 2020 states that a director stands in a fiduciary relationship towards the company and must act in the best interests of the company as a whole. Option B is the most tempting, but because the company is a separate legal person, the duty is owed to the company rather than to individual shareholders; employees and customers are interests directors may consider, not the party the duty is owed to.

questions.question: A public limited company (PLC) differs from a private limited company mainly in that a PLC:

options.b: Is owned by members who share profits according to patronage
options.d: Can invite the public to subscribe for its shares

questions.explanation: The main distinction is that a public company may offer its shares to the general public, for example through the stock exchange, while a private company cannot. Options C and A are shared by both types of company, and option B describes a cooperative society.

questions.question: A cooperative society mainly aims to:
questions.explanation: A cooperative is owned and controlled by members who join together to meet common needs, and surpluses are shared among members. Options B, C and A describe the goals of investor-owned public companies.

questions.question: A franchisor earns revenue mainly through:
questions.explanation: In a franchise, the franchisor lets the franchisee use its brand name and business system in return for an initial franchise fee and ongoing royalties, usually a share of sales. Option B is income from lending, and option D is a way of borrowing or lending money, not a franchise payment. Option C is wrong because a franchisee is an independent business, not a company paying the franchisor dividends.

questions.question: Which form of business organisation BEST combines limited liability with operational flexibility?
questions.explanation: A private limited company gives its owners limited liability while keeping ownership in a small group, with fewer disclosure and listing obligations than a public company, so it remains flexible to run. Options B and C are flexible but their owners usually have unlimited liability. Option D has limited liability but faces stricter rules, public disclosure and shareholder pressure, which reduce flexibility.

questions.question: The emergence of joint-stock companies was driven mainly by the need to:
questions.explanation: Joint-stock companies arose because ventures such as long-distance trade, railways and large factories needed more capital than one person or a few partners could provide, so the capital was divided into shares sold to many investors. Option A was not the purpose, option B is wrong because these companies were created under the law, and option C is wrong because spreading ownership actually made it harder for owners to control managers.

questions.question: The doctrine of separate legal entity mainly protects shareholders from:

options.d: Personal liability for the company's debts

questions.explanation: Because a registered company is a legal person separate from its members, its debts belong to the company, and shareholders with limited liability can lose at most what they invested. Option A is wrong because shareholders still bear losses through a fall in the value of their shares. Options B and C are not things the doctrine guards against.

questions.question: Modern corporate entities differ from early forms of business such as sole traders mainly because they have:

options.a: Only one owner who manages everything
options.b: A separate legal personality and limited liability for their members
options.d: No need to register with any authority

questions.explanation: A modern company is a legal person in its own right, separate from its shareholders, who usually have limited liability; this lets it raise capital from many investors and continue beyond the life of any owner. Option A describes a sole proprietorship, option C describes sole traders and ordinary partnerships, and option D is wrong because companies must be registered.

questions.question: An entrepreneur who needs to raise substantial capital while protecting the owners' personal assets from business debts should MOST likely choose a:

options.c: Business name registered to one person

questions.explanation: A limited liability company can bring in capital from several shareholders, and their liability is limited to their investment, so their personal assets are protected. Options A, B and C all expose the owners to unlimited personal liability and usually have limited ability to raise large capital.

questions.question: As at 2026, which body registers companies and business names in Nigeria under the Companies and Allied Matters Act (CAMA) 2020?
questions.explanation: The Corporate Affairs Commission administers CAMA 2020 and is responsible for registering companies, business names and incorporated trustees in Nigeria, which makes registration a legal factor in choosing an ownership form. Option A regulates the management profession, option C regulates banks and monetary policy, and option D regulates the capital market.

questions.question: A business owned and controlled by one person, who takes all the profits and bears all the risks, is a:
questions.explanation: A sole proprietorship has a single owner who makes all the decisions, keeps all the profit and carries all the losses. Option D has two or more owners, option B is a separate legal person owned by shareholders, and option C is owned by its members for mutual benefit.

questions.question: 'Unlimited liability', as it applies to a sole proprietor, means that:

options.a: The owner's losses are limited to the capital invested
options.b: The business can never be closed down
options.c: The owner's personal assets can be taken to pay the debts of the business
options.d: The owner can borrow without any limit

questions.explanation: With unlimited liability, there is no legal separation between the owner and the business, so creditors can claim the owner's house, car or savings to settle business debts. Option D confuses liability with borrowing capacity, option B confuses it with continuity, and option A describes limited liability.

questions.question: Ngozi runs a fashion shop as a sole proprietor. The business owes suppliers N3,000,000 but has assets worth only N1,000,000. Which statement is correct?

options.a: Only the shop's landlord is liable for the shortfall
options.b: The suppliers must write off the N2,000,000 by law
options.c: Ngozi can be made to pay the remaining N2,000,000 from her personal assets
options.d: Ngozi owes nothing beyond the N1,000,000 in the business

questions.explanation: A sole proprietor has unlimited liability, so the N2,000,000 shortfall can be recovered from her personal property. Option D would only be true if the business had limited liability, while options B and A have no legal basis.

questions.question: Which of the following is an ADVANTAGE of a sole proprietorship?

options.a: Continuity of existence after the owner's death
options.b: Easy access to large amounts of capital
options.c: Quick decision-making, because the owner does not need to consult anyone

questions.explanation: Because one person owns and controls the business, decisions can be made quickly and flexibly. Options B, D and A are actually features a sole proprietorship lacks: its capital is limited to what one person can raise, the owner's liability is unlimited, and it lacks continuity.

questions.question: Mr Adewale's well-run printing shop in Ibadan closes after his sudden death because nobody else is legally entitled to continue it. This illustrates the sole proprietorship's problem of:
questions.explanation: A sole proprietorship is not separate from its owner, so it usually ends when the owner dies or becomes incapacitated. Option D relates to companies whose profits are taxed and then dividends taxed again, option C is a feature of large companies, and option B does not apply since there are no shareholders.

questions.question: In Nigeria, a sole trader who wants to trade under a name other than his or her own true name should register a business name with the:
questions.explanation: Business names, companies, limited partnerships and limited liability partnerships are registered with the CAC under CAMA 2020. Option B regulates banks, option C regulates telecommunications, and option A handles privatisation of government enterprises.

questions.question: A partnership is best defined as:

options.a: The relationship between persons carrying on a business in common with a view of profit
options.b: A company owned by the government and private investors
options.c: A business owned by one person with the help of family members
options.d: An association of members who buy goods in bulk for their own use

questions.explanation: This is the classic definition of a partnership: two or more persons jointly carrying on a business to make profit. Option B describes a mixed or joint venture enterprise, option D describes a consumer cooperative, and option C remains a sole proprietorship.

questions.question: Under section 19 of CAMA 2020, an ordinary partnership formed to carry on business for profit may NOT have more than how many persons unless it is registered as a company or formed under another enactment?
questions.explanation: Section 19(1) of CAMA 2020 forbids an association or partnership of more than 20 persons carrying on business for profit unless it is registered as a company or formed under another law. Option D is the maximum membership of a private company, and options B and C are not the statutory limit.

questions.question: Section 19 of CAMA 2020 limits partnerships to 20 persons, but this limit does NOT apply to which of the following?

options.b: A partnership of legal practitioners or of accountants
options.d: A partnership of traders in a market

questions.explanation: Section 19(2) exempts partnerships of legal practitioners and of accountants, as well as registered cooperative societies, from the 20-person limit. Options D, C and A are ordinary trading partnerships and remain subject to the limit.

questions.question: A partner who contributes capital and shares in profits but takes no active part in managing the business is called a:
questions.explanation: A sleeping or dormant partner provides capital and shares profits but does not take part in day-to-day management. Option C takes part in running the business, option B lends only his or her name and usually contributes no capital, and option D is an officer of a company, not a type of partner.

questions.question: A person who allows his or her name to be used by a partnership to boost its reputation, but contributes no capital and takes no part in management, is a:
questions.explanation: A nominal partner lends only his or her name and goodwill to the firm and can still be held liable to outsiders who relied on that name. Option D contributes capital, option A contributes capital with liability limited to it, and option C manages the business.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT usually contained in a partnership deed?

options.a: The capital contributed by each partner
options.b: The ratio in which profits and losses are shared
options.c: The procedure for admitting or retiring a partner

questions.explanation: A partnership deed sets out the terms between partners, such as capital, profit-sharing ratio, interest on capital, drawings and admission or retirement of partners. A memorandum of association is a company's constitutional document, not part of a partnership deed. Options B, A and C are typical contents of a deed.

questions.question: Where partners have no written or oral agreement on how profits are to be shared, the general rule is that profits and losses are shared:
questions.explanation: In the absence of agreement, partnership law treats partners as entitled to share profits equally and to contribute equally to losses. Option A applies only if the partners agree to it, while options C and B have no basis in the default rule.

questions.question: In an ordinary partnership, 'joint and several liability' means that:

options.a: Partners are liable together, and each partner can also be held personally liable for all the firm's debts
options.b: No partner is personally liable for the firm's debts
options.c: Each partner is liable only for his or her own share of debts
options.d: Only the senior partner is liable for the firm's debts

questions.explanation: Creditors of an ordinary partnership can sue the partners together or any one of them for the full debt, leaving that partner to recover contributions from the others. Option C wrongly limits liability to a share, option D wrongly limits it to one partner, and option B describes limited liability.

questions.question: The principle of 'mutual agency' in a partnership means that:

options.a: Only a sleeping partner can sign contracts
options.b: The partnership cannot enter into contracts
options.c: Partners must employ agents to make contracts for them
options.d: Each partner can bind the firm and the other partners by acts done in the ordinary course of business

questions.explanation: Every partner is an agent of the firm and of the other partners for ordinary business, so a contract one partner makes binds all. Options C, A and B misdescribe or deny this authority.

questions.question: Under CAMA 2020, a limited partnership must have at least:

options.a: One general partner and one limited partner
options.b: Two limited partners and no general partner

questions.explanation: A limited partnership needs at least one general partner, who is liable for all the firm's debts, and at least one limited partner, whose liability is capped at the capital contributed. Options B and D leave out the general partner the law requires, and option C confuses the minimum with the 20-partner maximum.

questions.question: Funke is a limited partner in a registered limited partnership. She begins to take part in managing the firm and signs contracts on its behalf. Under CAMA 2020 the likely result is that she:

options.a: Is protected even more strongly from the firm's debts
options.b: Automatically becomes a director of a company
options.c: Becomes liable for the firm's debts incurred while she takes part in management
options.d: Loses her share of the profits permanently

questions.explanation: A limited partner's protection depends on staying out of management; if she takes part in management, she becomes liable for debts incurred during that period like a general partner. Options B, D and A do not describe this legal consequence.

questions.question: Which of the following is a feature of a limited liability partnership (LLP) under CAMA 2020?

options.a: Its partners have unlimited liability for all its debts
options.b: It is a separate legal person that can sue and be sued and hold property in its own name
options.c: It needs no registration with any authority
options.d: It must have more than 50 partners

questions.explanation: CAMA 2020 introduced the LLP as a body with its own legal personality and limited liability for partners, registered with the CAC. Option A describes an ordinary partnership, option D is not a requirement, and option C is wrong because LLPs must be registered.

questions.question: Under CAMA 2020, a limited liability partnership must have at least two designated partners who are individuals, and at least one of them must be:
questions.explanation: CAMA 2020 requires at least two designated partners who are individuals, with at least one resident in Nigeria, so there is always someone locally responsible for compliance. Options B, D and C are not requirements of the Act.

questions.question: The legal principle that a registered company is a separate legal person, distinct from its members, is associated with the case of:

options.a: Carlill v Carbolic Smoke Ball Co (1893)
options.d: Salomon v Salomon and Co Ltd (1897)

questions.explanation: Salomon v Salomon established that once a company is properly incorporated it is a legal person separate from its shareholders, even a dominant one. Option B is the key negligence case, option A concerns offer and acceptance in contract, and option C concerns who may sue for wrongs done to a company.

questions.question: The feature of a company by which it continues to exist even when its shareholders die or sell their shares is called:
questions.explanation: Perpetual succession means the company's life does not depend on the life or membership of its shareholders; it continues until it is wound up. Option B limits members' losses to their unpaid shares, option D is a partnership principle, and option A is a management principle.

questions.question: In a company limited by shares, the liability of a member is limited to:

options.a: The amount he or she agreed to contribute on winding up
options.b: Twice the nominal value of his or her shares
options.c: The total debts of the company
options.d: The amount, if any, unpaid on the shares he or she holds

questions.explanation: In a company limited by shares, once a member has fully paid for the shares, he or she cannot be asked to contribute more to the company's debts. Option C describes unlimited liability, option A describes a company limited by guarantee, and option B has no legal basis.

questions.question: Under section 21 of CAMA 2020, which of the following is a type of company that may be registered?
questions.explanation: Section 21 recognises companies limited by shares, companies limited by guarantee and unlimited companies. Options D and C are registered with the CAC but are not companies, and option B is formed under cooperative law.

questions.question: In a company limited by guarantee, a member's liability is limited to:

options.a: Nothing at all in any circumstance
options.b: The amount he or she undertook to contribute to the company's assets if it is wound up
options.c: All the company's debts without limit
options.d: The amount unpaid on his or her shares

questions.explanation: Members of a guarantee company promise to contribute a stated amount if the company is wound up, and that guarantee sets the limit of their liability. Option D describes a company limited by shares, option A ignores the guarantee, and option C describes an unlimited company.

questions.question: A group of alumni wants to register a body in Lagos to promote education and award scholarships, with no profits distributed to members. The most suitable type of company is a:
questions.explanation: Companies limited by guarantee are formed to promote objects such as education, charity, science or culture, and their income is not distributed to members. Options A and B are designed to make and distribute profits to shareholders, and option D would expose members to unlimited liability.

questions.question: In an unlimited company, if the company's liabilities exceed its assets on winding up:

options.a: Members lose only the amount they guaranteed
options.b: Creditors cannot recover anything from members
options.c: Members lose only the amount unpaid on their shares
options.d: Members can be required to contribute from their personal assets to settle the shortfall

questions.explanation: Members of an unlimited company have no limit on their liability, so creditors can reach their personal property through contributions on winding up. Option C applies to companies limited by shares, option A to companies limited by guarantee, and option B contradicts unlimited liability.

questions.question: Under CAMA 2020, the minimum issued share capital of a PRIVATE company is:
questions.explanation: Section 27(2)(a) of CAMA 2020 sets the minimum issued share capital at N100,000 for a private company and N2,000,000 for a public company. Option B is the public company figure, while options A and C are not the statutory minimum.

questions.question: Under CAMA 2020, the minimum issued share capital of a PUBLIC company is:
questions.explanation: Section 27(2)(a) of CAMA 2020 requires a public company to have a minimum issued share capital of N2,000,000. Option A is the private company minimum, while options D and C do not match the Act.

questions.question: Which of the following was introduced by CAMA 2020?

options.a: One person may form a private company (a single-member company)
options.b: A private company must have at least seven members
options.c: Partnerships may have unlimited numbers of partners
options.d: Public companies may have only one member

questions.explanation: Section 18(2) of CAMA 2020 allows one person to form and incorporate a private company, which was not possible under the previous law. Option B does not reflect the law, option C contradicts the 20-person limit in section 19, and option D is wrong because a public company needs at least two members.

questions.question: Under CAMA 2020, the maximum number of members of a PRIVATE company (joint holders of a share counting as one) is:
questions.explanation: A private company's membership is limited to 50, with joint holders of shares treated as one member. Option A is the limit for ordinary partnerships, option B is not the rule, and option D describes a public company, which has no maximum.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a PRIVATE company from a PUBLIC company under CAMA 2020?

options.a: A private company is owned by government, while a public company is owned by private investors
options.b: A private company restricts the transfer of its shares and may not invite the public to subscribe for its shares, while a public company may
options.c: A private company must have at least two members, while a public company may have one
options.d: A private company has unlimited liability, while a public company has limited liability

questions.explanation: Private companies must restrict share transfers and cannot offer shares or debentures to the public, while public companies can raise capital from the public. Option D confuses private status with liability, option C reverses the membership rules, and option A confuses 'public company' with a government-owned enterprise.

questions.question: Under CAMA 2020, a small company is NOT required to:

options.a: Register with the Corporate Affairs Commission
options.b: Keep any accounting records at all

questions.explanation: Section 402 of CAMA 2020 exempts small companies from the requirement to appoint auditors, reducing compliance costs for small businesses. Options B, A and C remain necessary: every company must keep records, be registered with the CAC and have at least one member.

questions.question: Which of the following CAMA 2020 provisions reduces the cost of running a small private company?

options.a: It must appoint at least three independent directors
options.b: It is not mandatory for a small company to appoint a company secretary
options.c: It must hold an annual general meeting every quarter
options.d: It must list its shares on the Nigerian Exchange

questions.explanation: Section 330 of CAMA 2020 makes the appointment of a company secretary optional for small companies, and section 237 also excuses small companies from holding AGMs. Option A is a public company requirement, option C is not a requirement for any company, and option D applies only to listed public companies.

questions.question: Under CAMA 2020, a public company must have at least how many independent directors?
questions.explanation: Section 275 of CAMA 2020 requires every public company to have at least three independent directors who meet stated criteria, to strengthen board objectivity. Options C, B and D do not match the statutory minimum.

questions.question: Under section 307 of CAMA 2020, a person may NOT be a director of more than how many PUBLIC companies at the same time?
questions.explanation: Section 307(1) of CAMA 2020 limits a person to directorships of not more than five public companies, so directors can give enough time to each board. Options D, B and A do not match the limit in the Act.

questions.question: The memorandum of association of a company differs from its articles of association mainly because the memorandum:

options.a: States the company's basic constitution, such as its name, objects or business, liability of members and share capital
options.b: Contains the detailed internal rules for meetings and appointment of directors
options.c: Is a contract among partners of a firm
options.d: Is the annual report sent to shareholders

questions.explanation: The memorandum sets out the company's fundamental details and its relationship with the outside world, while the articles are the internal regulations on matters such as meetings, directors and share transfers. Option B describes the articles, option C describes a partnership deed, and option D describes annual accounts.

questions.question: Which of the following is an ADVANTAGE of a public limited company over a sole proprietorship?

options.a: It is cheaper and quicker to form
options.b: It can raise large amounts of capital by offering shares to the public
options.c: Its owner can keep all business information secret
options.d: One person makes all decisions without consultation

questions.explanation: A public company can invite the public to buy its shares, which allows it to raise far more capital than one person could. Options C, A and D are advantages of a sole proprietorship, not of a public company, which must disclose information and is costlier to form.

questions.question: Which of the following is a DISADVANTAGE of a public limited company?

options.b: It ends when a major shareholder dies
options.d: It must disclose a great deal of information and comply with heavy regulation

questions.explanation: Public companies face extensive disclosure, reporting and governance rules, and ownership is often separated from control. Option C is wrong because shareholders have limited liability, option B ignores perpetual succession, and option A is wrong because public companies typically employ professional managers.

questions.question: A voluntary association of people who join together on equal terms to meet their common economic needs through a jointly owned and democratically controlled enterprise is a:
questions.explanation: A cooperative is owned and controlled by its members and run for their mutual benefit rather than for outside investors. Option B is owned by shareholders seeking returns, option C has one owner, and option A is a government enterprise created by statute.

questions.question: In a cooperative society, voting at general meetings is usually based on the principle of:

options.a: One member, one vote, regardless of shares held
options.c: Votes in proportion to years of membership

questions.explanation: Democratic member control means each member has one vote, however much capital he or she has contributed. Option B applies in companies, while options C and D are not cooperative principles.

questions.question: A cooperative society usually distributes its surplus to members:

options.a: Only to the chairman and committee
options.b: In proportion to the number of shares each member holds, like a company
options.c: In proportion to the business each member did with the society (patronage)
options.d: Never, because cooperatives cannot have a surplus

questions.explanation: Cooperatives often return surplus as a patronage dividend, so members who buy or sell more through the society get more. Option A contradicts democratic control, option B describes company dividends, and option D is wrong because cooperatives can earn a surplus.

questions.question: Staff of a Lagos hospital contribute part of their salaries each month into a society that grants them low-interest loans. This is an example of a:
questions.explanation: A thrift and credit cooperative encourages members to save regularly and lends to them at low interest. Option D is formed by producers to produce jointly, option A buys goods in bulk for resale to members, and option C helps producers sell their output.

questions.question: Cocoa farmers in Ondo State form a society to collect, grade and sell their cocoa together to get better prices from exporters. This is a:
questions.explanation: A marketing cooperative helps producers sell their output jointly, gaining bargaining power and better prices. Option A buys goods for members' own consumption, option D focuses on savings and loans, and option C is owned by government.

questions.question: A business enterprise that is owned and controlled wholly or mainly by government to provide goods or services to the public is a:
questions.explanation: Public enterprises, such as statutory corporations and government-owned companies, are owned and controlled by government. Option A is owned by private shareholders even though its shares are offered to the public, option C is owned by its members, and option D is owned by private partners.

questions.question: A public enterprise established by a specific Act of the legislature, which defines its powers, functions and management, is called a:
questions.explanation: A statutory corporation is created by its own law, which sets its objectives and powers. Option B is incorporated by private persons under CAMA, option D has no special statute, and option A is registered under CAMA by private partners.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT usually a reason why governments set up public enterprises?

options.a: To control strategic sectors of the economy
options.b: To prevent private monopolies from exploiting consumers
options.c: To provide essential services that private firms may neglect
options.d: To maximise profits for private shareholders

questions.explanation: Public enterprises are created to serve public interest goals such as providing essential services, controlling strategic industries and protecting consumers. Maximising profit for private shareholders is the goal of private companies. Options C, A and B are typical reasons for public enterprises.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes PRIVATISATION from COMMERCIALISATION of a public enterprise?

options.a: Both mean closing down the enterprise
options.b: Both mean converting the enterprise into a cooperative
options.c: Privatisation transfers ownership to private investors, while commercialisation keeps government ownership but requires the enterprise to run on commercial, profit-making lines
options.d: Privatisation keeps government ownership, while commercialisation sells the enterprise to private investors

questions.explanation: In privatisation, government sells all or part of its shares to private investors; in commercialisation, government remains the owner but the enterprise must cover its costs and operate like a business. Option D reverses the two, and options A and B do not describe either policy.

questions.question: Which of the following is a common PROBLEM of public enterprises in Nigeria?

options.a: Unlimited personal liability of the managers
options.b: A legal ban on receiving government funds
options.c: Political interference in appointments and decisions
options.d: Too much pressure from private shareholders for dividends

questions.explanation: Public enterprises often suffer from political interference, bureaucracy and weak accountability, which reduce efficiency. Option D relates to private companies, option A is not a feature of public enterprises, and option B is wrong because they usually depend on government funding.

questions.question: An arrangement in which a business owner grants another party the right to sell its products under its brand name and business system, in return for fees or royalties, is a:
questions.explanation: In a franchise, the franchisor licenses its brand and methods to a franchisee, who pays initial fees and ongoing royalties. Option A involves co-ownership of one business, option C is member-owned for mutual benefit, and option D combines two firms into one.

questions.question: When choosing a form of business ownership, which of the following considerations is mainly LEGAL?

options.a: The managerial skills available to the owners
options.b: The extent of the owners' liability for business debts
options.c: The amount of capital the owners can raise
options.d: How quickly decisions can be made

questions.explanation: Liability is a legal consideration, since it depends on whether the law treats the business as separate from its owners. Option C is a financial consideration, while options D and A are managerial considerations.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: When managers sacrifice some short-term profit to build long-term trust with employees, customers and the community, this reflects:
questions.explanation: Stakeholder capitalism holds that a business should create value for all its stakeholders, not only its owners, even if that means giving up some profit in the short run. Option B and option C both treat maximising returns to shareholders as the main goal, which is the opposite of what the managers are doing here.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Agency costs in a company arise mainly because of:

options.c: Divergence of interests between owners (principals) and managers (agents)

questions.explanation: Agency costs are the costs of monitoring and aligning managers who may pursue their own interests instead of the owners'. Options A, D and B are external conditions in the business environment and do not create the owner-manager conflict that agency theory describes.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: An independent non-executive director on a company board mainly enhances:
questions.explanation: Independent non-executive directors are not part of management, so they can objectively oversee and challenge executives on behalf of the company. Option B is the opposite of their purpose, since they act as a check on executive power, and options A and D are the day-to-day work of management.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Ethical decision-making based on achieving "the greatest good for the greatest number" aligns with:
questions.explanation: Utilitarianism judges an action by its consequences and favours the choice that produces the most benefit for the most people. Option C judges actions by duties and rules regardless of outcome, and option A focuses on what benefits the decision-maker personally.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: A transformational leader differs from a transactional leader by focusing on:

options.a: Inspiring followers with a vision to achieve more than expected

questions.explanation: Transformational leaders inspire and motivate followers to go beyond expected results, often through a compelling vision and charisma. Option B is the defining feature of transactional leadership, which motivates through exchanges of rewards and punishments.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) aligns most closely with:
questions.explanation: CSR asks businesses to consider employees, customers, communities and the environment, which is the central idea of stakeholder theory. Option B holds that a firm's only social responsibility is to make profit for its owners, and option C deals with the owner-manager relationship.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: An autocratic leadership style may be most effective when:

options.b: Urgent decisions are needed in a crisis

questions.explanation: In a crisis there is little time for consultation, so a leader making quick, firm decisions alone can be effective. Option C calls for a participative style that draws ideas from the team, and option D contradicts autocracy, which centralises decisions in the leader.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Corporate governance failure often results in:
questions.explanation: When boards fail to oversee management, problems like manipulated accounts and hidden losses are common outcomes, as many corporate scandals show. Options B, A and C are positive outcomes linked with good governance, not its failure.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Ethical compliance differs from ethics in general because compliance is mainly:
questions.explanation: Compliance means obeying laws, regulations and codes that are enforced, while ethics goes further to what is morally right even where no law requires it. Option A describes ethics, which often goes beyond what is compulsory, and option B describes ethics as a field of study.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Leadership ethics most directly influence:
questions.explanation: When leaders act with honesty, fairness and accountability, employees and other stakeholders come to trust the organisation. Options D, C and A are economy-wide variables outside a leader's ethical conduct.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Ethical leadership mainly enhances an organisation's:
questions.explanation: Leaders who consistently act with integrity build the organisation's good name with customers, investors and regulators, a valuable form of reputation capital. Options D, C and B are economic conditions that ethical behaviour does not directly create.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Stakeholder mapping is mainly used to:

options.c: Classify stakeholders by their power or influence and their interest in the organisation

questions.explanation: Stakeholder mapping identifies the people and groups affected by an organisation and ranks them by how much influence and interest they have, so managers know whom to consult, inform or monitor closely. Option A is a dividend decision, option B is a routine HR or accounting task, and option D is a financing decision; none of them involves analysing stakeholders.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Social responsibility reporting improves:
questions.explanation: Social responsibility reporting discloses how a company affects society and the environment, which makes its conduct more open and lets stakeholders hold it to account. Options A and B are economy-wide conditions that a company's report cannot change. Option D is illegal and is exactly what openness and disclosure discourage.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Internal audit strengthens:
questions.explanation: Internal audit is an independent check within the organisation that tests whether controls, procedures and records are working properly, so it strengthens operational control and helps detect errors and fraud. Option A and option D are marketing decisions, and option B is set by the economy and monetary policy, not by a firm's auditors.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Corporate failure is often linked to:
questions.explanation: Weak governance, such as poor board oversight, lack of accountability and unchecked management, allows bad decisions and fraud to go unnoticed until the company collapses. Options A, B and C are generally signs of a well-run, responsible company, not causes of failure.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Which combination BEST explains why management is often regarded as a semi-profession rather than a full profession in many countries?

options.a: Absence of a profit motive and of ethical codes
options.b: Lack of theoretical knowledge and formal training
options.c: Dependence on intuition rather than principles
options.d: Free entry into practice and no compulsory licence or statutory regulation

questions.explanation: Full professions such as medicine and law restrict entry: you cannot practise without a recognised qualification and a licence from a regulating body. In many countries anyone can become a manager without such a licence, which is the main reason management is called a semi-profession. Option B is wrong because management has a large body of theory and many formal training programmes, and option C is wrong because managers apply established principles. In Nigeria the argument is weaker, since a statutory body regulates the management profession there.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: A profession differs from an ordinary occupation mainly because it:

options.a: Enforces discipline through a recognised professional body

questions.explanation: A profession has a recognised body that sets entry standards, issues licences, enforces a code of conduct and disciplines members who break it. Option B is wrong because no profession guarantees income, and many occupations also require long experience (option C) or dealing with people (option D).

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Which situation represents a breach of professional integrity under the Nigerian Institute of Management (NIM) code of ethics?

options.a: Manipulating reports to protect management's image

questions.explanation: Integrity and honesty require managers to present facts truthfully, so altering reports to make management look good is a clear breach. Options B, C and D are examples of good professional conduct: being honest about one's limits, avoiding conflicts of interest and keeping skills current.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: A major objective of corporate governance is to resolve conflicts between:
questions.explanation: In a company the shareholders own the business but managers run it, and managers may pursue their own interests instead of the owners' (the agency problem). Corporate governance sets up boards, controls and disclosure so that managers are held to account to the owners. Options B, C and D are other relationships that governance may touch, but they are not its central concern.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Under the Nigerian Code of Corporate Governance (NCCG) 2018, requiring independent non-executive directors on the board is mainly intended to:

options.b: Strengthen accountability and oversight of management

questions.explanation: Independent directors have no management role or close ties to the company, so they can question executives objectively and protect the interests of shareholders and other stakeholders. Option C is the opposite, since independence is meant to check executive power. Options A and D are not aims of board independence.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Which leadership theory argues that no single leadership style is effective in every situation?
questions.explanation: Contingency theory holds that the best way to lead depends on the situation, such as the task, the followers and the leader's position. Option B looks for inborn qualities that all leaders share, and option C looks for the behaviours that make leaders successful, so both seek general answers. Option D focuses on a leader's personal appeal rather than on matching style to situation.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: A leader who changes style according to the maturity (readiness) of followers is applying:
questions.explanation: Situational leadership theory says leaders should adjust how much direction and support they give according to how willing and able followers are to do a task. Option B explains leadership by inborn qualities, while options C and D are fixed styles that do not change with followers' maturity.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: As at 2026, which body is legally charged with regulating and controlling the practice of management as a profession in Nigeria?

options.b: The Financial Reporting Council of Nigeria
options.d: The Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nigeria

questions.explanation: The Nigerian Institute of Management (Chartered) is the statutory body that sets standards for the management profession, keeps a register of members and regulates management practice in Nigeria. Option A registers companies and business names, option B oversees financial reporting and corporate governance codes, and option D regulates accountants, not managers in general.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: The Nigerian Institute of Management was given its statutory regulatory role by:

options.a: The Companies and Allied Matters Act 2020
options.b: The Nigerian Code of Corporate Governance 2018
options.c: A resolution of its members without any law
options.d: The Nigerian Institute of Management (Establishment) Act No. 14 of 2003

questions.explanation: NIM became a statutory regulator through an Act of the National Assembly, Act No. 14 of 2003, which empowers it to set standards for, and regulate, the management profession. Option A is the general law on companies and business registration. Option B is a governance code for organisations, not a law creating a professional body, and option C would not give NIM legal power over non-members.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of a profession?

options.a: A guaranteed high income for every member
options.b: Extensive training to acquire specialised knowledge
options.c: A licence or certification to practise
options.d: A code of ethics and code of conduct

questions.explanation: The usual marks of a profession are specialised training, skills from practice, a licence or certification, a code of ethics with a code of conduct, and standards of practice. Income is not one of them, because no profession can promise its members high earnings. Options B, C and D are all genuine characteristics.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: A permission granted by a professional body or government authority to individuals who meet specific qualifications, allowing them to practise a profession, is called a:
questions.explanation: A licence or certification is formal permission to practise, given only to people who meet the required qualifications. Option A sets out practical rules of behaviour, option C is a measure of quality of practice, and option D states the broad moral principles of the profession; none of them is permission to practise.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: In a profession, the document that translates broad ethical principles into practical guidelines for behaviour, such as obeying the law and avoiding conflicts of interest, is the:
questions.explanation: A code of conduct turns values into specific rules on how members should behave in everyday situations. Option A is close but it states the overarching moral principles and values, while the code of conduct spells out how to apply them. Options B and C deal with permission to practise and quality measures, not behaviour.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Criteria or measures of the quality of practice or performance, such as units of measurement, building regulations or the ISO 9000 quality management system, are known as:
questions.explanation: Standards are agreed benchmarks for judging the quality of work or performance, and ISO 9000 is a well-known example for quality management. Option A gives permission to practise, option B states moral principles, and option D is the document that shows a company has been registered.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Which of the following is a reason commonly given for regarding management as a semi-profession rather than a full profession?

options.a: Management has no organised body of knowledge
options.d: In many countries people can work as managers without a compulsory licence or a specific required qualification

questions.explanation: Full professions such as law and medicine bar anyone without the required qualification and licence from practising, but in many countries people become managers without either, so entry is open. Options A and B are false, since management has well-developed theories and many degree and training programmes. Option C is true of management but is not why it falls short of a full profession.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an argument for calling management a semi-profession?

options.a: Entry into management is generally not restricted
options.b: Practising as a manager usually does not require a licence
options.c: There is no single qualification every manager must hold
options.d: Management has a systematic body of principles that can be taught

questions.explanation: Having a teachable body of principles is one of the features that management shares with full professions, so it supports treating management as a profession rather than counting against it. Options A, B and C are the usual reasons why management is seen as only a semi-profession.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Corporate governance is BEST defined as:

options.a: The system by which organisations are directed and controlled
options.b: The process of selling a company's products
options.c: The day-to-day supervision of factory workers
options.d: The preparation of a company's tax returns

questions.explanation: Corporate governance is the framework of rules, policies and processes by which organisations are directed and controlled, covering the roles of the board, management and shareholders. Option B is marketing, option C is operational supervision, and option D is a tax and accounting task.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the core principles of corporate governance?
questions.explanation: The core principles of corporate governance are responsibility, accountability, transparency and fairness. Secrecy is the opposite of transparency, because good governance requires openness so that shareholders and other stakeholders can judge how the company is run. Options A, B and C are all core principles.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Good corporate governance is important to modern business organisations mainly because it:

options.a: Protects the interests of shareholders and other stakeholders and builds investor trust
options.b: Guarantees that the company will make a profit
options.c: Gives managers unlimited power over company resources
options.d: Removes the need for external audit

questions.explanation: Good governance holds management accountable, improves disclosure and reduces the risk of fraud and abuse, which protects stakeholders and makes investors more willing to commit funds. Option B is wrong because no system can guarantee profit. Options C and D describe exactly the lack of checks that good governance is meant to prevent.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Which body issued the Nigerian Code of Corporate Governance (NCCG) 2018?

options.b: The Financial Reporting Council of Nigeria

questions.explanation: The NCCG 2018 was issued by the Financial Reporting Council of Nigeria and unveiled in January 2019 as the national code of governance principles and practices. Option A registers companies under CAMA, option C regulates the management profession, and option D issues rules for banks; none of them issued this code.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: The compliance approach adopted by the Nigerian Code of Corporate Governance (NCCG) 2018 is known as:
questions.explanation: Under the NCCG 2018, companies are expected to apply the principles in a way that suits their size and business and then explain how their practices achieve the purpose of those principles. Option A is close and is used in some other countries, but it allows a company not to comply as long as it explains why, which is not the NCCG 2018 approach. Options B and D do not describe the code at all.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: The main aim of the Nigerian Code of Corporate Governance (NCCG) 2018 is to:

options.a: Fix the prices of goods sold by Nigerian companies
options.b: Register new companies and business names
options.c: Promote transparency, integrity and public trust in Nigerian organisations
options.d: Set the exchange rate of the naira

questions.explanation: The NCCG 2018 sets out standard principles and practices of corporate governance, including requirements on board structure, board and committee meetings and disclosure, in order to promote transparency, integrity and public trust. Option A is not a governance matter, option B is the work of the Corporate Affairs Commission, and option D is a monetary policy matter.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the values in the Nigerian Institute of Management (NIM) code of ethics?
questions.explanation: The NIM code of ethics includes integrity and honesty, transparency, fairness, accountability, responsibility, effectiveness and efficiency. Favouritism is the opposite of fairness, which requires managers to be impartial and avoid discrimination. Options B, C and D are all values in the code.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: In the Nigerian Institute of Management (NIM) code of ethics, the obligation to give an account of a job done or of how a responsibility was carried out is called:
questions.explanation: Accountability means a manager must be able to explain and answer for how a task or responsibility was handled. Option B is close but means openness in dealings, not answering for results. Option C is about using the least resources, and option D is about being impartial.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: A manager who accomplishes a task using the least possible resources is demonstrating:
questions.explanation: Efficiency means getting a task done with the minimum use of resources such as time, money and materials. Option A is the most tempting, but effectiveness means achieving the desired objective or result, whatever resources it takes. Options C and D relate to openness and answering for one's actions.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: In its basic meaning, a profession is best described as:
questions.explanation: At its simplest, a profession is the regular work or occupation a person does, such as teaching, medicine, law or engineering. Option A is a single deal, not ongoing work, while D and C describe a hobby and a form of ownership rather than an occupation.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Which of the following pairs correctly matches a profession with its practitioner?
questions.explanation: Architecture is practised by an architect, just as law is practised by a lawyer and medicine by a doctor. Options A, B and C all pair a profession with the practitioner of a different profession.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of a profession?

options.b: Extensive training to acquire specialised knowledge
options.c: Membership passed down automatically from parent to child
options.d: A code of ethics and code of conduct

questions.explanation: Entry into a profession depends on training, demonstrated expertise and licensing, not on family inheritance. Options A, B and D are all recognised characteristics of a profession.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
