questions.question: As a characteristic of a profession, the 'extensive preparation to acquire specialised knowledge, usually combining education and practical instruction' refers to:
questions.explanation: Training is the extensive preparation through which members acquire specialised knowledge, and most professions require both education and training. Option B is the permission that follows qualification, while C and D govern quality and behaviour after entry.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Skills or expertise, as a characteristic of a profession, result mainly from:

options.d: Experience and practice in applying knowledge

questions.explanation: Professional skill or expertise grows out of experience and practice, that is, repeatedly applying knowledge to real tasks. Options A, B and C may give someone a position or membership but do not by themselves create expertise.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: In the context of a profession, ethics refers to:

options.a: The fees charged for professional services
options.b: The measurement units used in quality control
options.c: The minimum educational qualification for entry
options.d: The principles an organisation sets for itself in its internal and external dealings

questions.explanation: Ethics are the principles an organisation sets for itself in dealing with people inside and outside it, and a code of ethics states the overarching moral principles and values. Option C describes an entry requirement and B describes standards, not ethics.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes a code of ethics from a code of conduct?

options.a: A code of ethics states overarching moral principles, while a code of conduct gives practical guidelines for behaviour
options.b: A code of ethics sets quality measures, while a code of conduct sets licensing fees
options.c: A code of ethics is enforced by courts, while a code of conduct is purely voluntary
options.d: A code of ethics applies only to employees, while a code of conduct applies only to directors

questions.explanation: The code of ethics provides the broad moral principles and values, and the code of conduct translates them into specific behavioural guidelines. Options B, C and D invent differences in enforcement, coverage and content that do not define the two codes.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Criteria or measures for the quality of practice or performance in a profession are known as:
questions.explanation: Standards are the criteria used to judge the quality of practice or performance, for example units of measurement, building regulations and quality management systems. Option D concerns moral principles and C concerns permission to practise.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a standard as a characteristic of professional practice?
questions.explanation: ISO 9000 is a quality management system standard, a recognised measure of the quality of practice. Other examples of standards are units of measurement and building regulations; options A, D and B do not measure quality of performance.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: 'The process of designing and maintaining an environment in which individuals, working together in groups, efficiently accomplish selected aims' is a definition of:
questions.explanation: This is the classic Koontz-and-Weihrich definition of management: creating and maintaining an environment in which people working in groups achieve chosen aims efficiently. Option B concerns how organisations are directed and controlled, and A is the process of influencing people towards goals.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Management is regarded as a profession in Nigeria mainly because it involves:

options.a: Only a university degree with no ethical code
options.b: Education, training, skills, ethical codes of conduct and a statutory regulatory body
options.c: Hereditary entry, informal skills and no regulator
options.d: Registration of a company with the Corporate Affairs Commission

questions.explanation: Management qualifies as a profession in Nigeria because it has education, specialised training, skills, ethical codes of conduct and a statutory body that regulates it. Option C lacks the defining features, A leaves out ethics and regulation, and D describes company registration, not a profession.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: The statutory body established by an Act of the National Assembly to regulate and control the management profession in Nigeria is the:
questions.explanation: The Nigerian Institute of Management (NIM) is the statutory body that regulates and controls the practice of management in Nigeria. Option C registers companies, A oversees financial reporting and issued the corporate governance code, and B is the body for lawyers.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: The Act of the National Assembly that established the Nigerian Institute of Management as the regulator of the management profession was passed in:
questions.explanation: The Nigerian Institute of Management was given statutory backing by Act 14 of 2003 to regulate the management profession. Option A is the year of the Nigerian Code of Corporate Governance, and D is the year of independence.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: A key function of the Nigerian Institute of Management (NIM) is to:

options.a: Determine standards for the management profession and control its practice in Nigeria
options.b: Register business names and incorporate companies
options.d: Set the monetary policy rate for banks

questions.explanation: NIM determines the standards of the management profession and controls the practice of management in Nigeria. Option B is the work of the Corporate Affairs Commission and D is the work of the Central Bank of Nigeria.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Under the NIM Code of Ethics, 'openness in dealings' describes the value of:
questions.explanation: Transparency means openness in dealings, so that relevant information and decisions are visible to those affected. Option D is about impartiality, B is about using the least resources, and C is the duty to perform a task.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Under the NIM Code of Ethics, being impartial and showing no favouritism or discrimination describes:
questions.explanation: Fairness means being impartial, with no favouritism or discrimination in how people are treated. Option D is openness in dealings, B is the obligation to give account, and A is achieving objectives.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes responsibility from accountability?

options.a: Responsibility applies only to directors, while accountability applies only to junior staff
options.b: Responsibility and accountability mean exactly the same thing
options.c: Responsibility is the duty to perform a task, while accountability is the obligation to give account for how it was done
options.d: Responsibility is about using the least resources, while accountability is about achieving results

questions.explanation: Responsibility is the obligation or duty to perform a task, and accountability is the obligation to answer for how that task or responsibility was carried out. Option D confuses them with efficiency and effectiveness, and B ignores the difference between doing and answering for.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: In managerial terms, effectiveness differs from efficiency because effectiveness means:

options.c: Accomplishing a task with the least resources
options.d: Achieving the objectives or desired results

questions.explanation: Effectiveness is about achieving objectives or desired results, while efficiency is about accomplishing a task with the least resources. Option C is the definition of efficiency, the most common mix-up, and A describes fairness.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Two Lagos bakeries each produce 2,000 loaves a day as planned. Bakery A spends N180,000 on inputs daily, while Bakery B spends N240,000 for the same output and quality. Compared with Bakery B, Bakery A is:
questions.explanation: Both bakeries achieve the same target output, so they are equally effective; Bakery A uses fewer resources for that output, so it is more efficient. Option C wrongly claims a difference in results and gets efficiency backwards, and B wrongly treats lower cost as a difference in results achieved.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: A procurement manager at an Abuja agency awards a N12 million supply contract to a company owned by his cousin even though another qualified bidder quoted less. Which NIM value is most directly violated?
questions.explanation: Fairness requires impartiality with no favouritism, and favouring a relative's company over a cheaper qualified bidder is favouritism. Option D could also suffer from paying more, but the core ethical breach is the lack of impartiality; C and A are not the values at stake.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: A Nigerian state agency publishes the full list of bidders, bid prices and the winning bid for every contract on its website. This practice best demonstrates:
questions.explanation: Publishing bids and outcomes openly is transparency, which means openness in dealings. Options B and D relate to resources and results, and C is the duty to perform a task, not openness about it.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the values in the NIM Code of Ethics?
questions.explanation: The NIM values include integrity and honesty, transparency, fairness, accountability, responsibility, effectiveness and efficiency; profit at any cost is not an ethical value and would conflict with several of them. Options A, C and D are all on the list.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Which set lists the four key principles of corporate governance?
questions.explanation: The key principles of corporate governance are responsibility, accountability, transparency and fairness. Option D lists the management functions, B the marketing mix, and A the characteristics of a profession.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: The Nigerian Code of Corporate Governance (NCCG) 2018 states:

options.a: The minimum wage for Nigerian workers
options.b: The tax rates payable by Nigerian companies
options.c: The standard of principles and practices for corporate governance in Nigerian public and private organisations
options.d: The procedure for registering business names in Nigeria

questions.explanation: NCCG 2018 sets out the standard of principles and practices for corporate governance in Nigerian organisations. Options B, D and A are matters covered by tax law, company registration rules and labour law respectively.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Which of the following does the Nigerian Code of Corporate Governance 2018 set requirements for?

options.a: Recruitment of junior staff and annual leave
options.b: Board structure, board and committee meetings, and disclosure reports
options.d: Exchange rates, interest rates and inflation

questions.explanation: The Code sets requirements for board structure, board and committee meetings, and disclosure reports. Option C is the marketing mix, D is macroeconomic policy, and A is routine HR administration.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Companies applying the Nigerian Code of Corporate Governance 2018 are expected to follow which approach?
questions.explanation: NCCG 2018 uses an 'apply and explain' approach: companies apply the principles in the way that suits their business and explain how they have done so. Option B is the different approach used in some older codes, where a company may choose not to comply if it explains why.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: The board of a Nigerian plc proposes that its Managing Director/CEO should also become Chairman of the Board. Under NCCG 2018 this proposal is:

options.a: Required by the Code for all listed companies
options.b: Inconsistent with the Code, because the Chairman and MD/CEO roles should be held by different persons
options.c: Permitted only if the CEO holds more than half of the shares
options.d: Recommended by the Code, because it speeds up decisions

questions.explanation: NCCG 2018 requires the positions of Chairman and MD/CEO to be held by different people, and the Chairman should be a non-executive director. Separating the roles prevents one person from both running the company and supervising that work, so options D, A and C are wrong.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Under NCCG 2018, the board of directors should meet at least:

options.d: Only at the annual general meeting

questions.explanation: The Code requires the board to meet at least once in every quarter, so that directors can oversee the company regularly. Options B, C and D would leave the board unable to give regular oversight.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Under NCCG 2018, a company should have a framework that allows staff and others to report unethical conduct confidentially and without suffering harm. This is a:
questions.explanation: A whistleblowing framework lets people report unethical conduct or violations while keeping their identity confidential and protecting them from detriment. Option A is the board's review of its own performance, and B and D deal with profits and leadership continuity.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Under NCCG 2018, in addition to the board's annual evaluation of itself, an evaluation by an independent external consultant should be carried out at least once every:
questions.explanation: The Code expects an annual board evaluation plus an external evaluation by an independent consultant at least every three years. Options A and C are too infrequent for independent review, and B is more often than the Code requires.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: How many key principles does the Nigerian Code of Corporate Governance 2018 contain?
questions.explanation: NCCG 2018 contains 28 principles grouped under areas such as the board, business conduct and ethics, relationship with shareholders, sustainability, transparency and assurance. Option A is the number of general corporate governance principles (responsibility, accountability, transparency, fairness), a common mix-up.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Ethics and responsibility in managerial practice require managers to:

options.a: Set standards through integrity, fairness and transparency and consider all stakeholders, not only themselves and shareholders
options.b: Avoid setting standards so that staff can decide freely
options.c: Serve shareholders only and ignore employees and customers
options.d: Maximise their own bonuses before any other goal

questions.explanation: Ethical managers set standards through integrity, fairness and transparency and make decisions that benefit other stakeholders as well, including employees, customers and the operating environment. Option C looks only at shareholders and D looks only at the manager.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: The process in which an individual influences other group members towards the attainment of group or organisational goals is called:
questions.explanation: Leadership is the process of influencing group members towards achieving group or organisational goals. Option A is the system for directing and controlling organisations, while D and C are characteristics of a profession.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: The leadership theory which holds that people are born with innate abilities such as intelligence, charisma and courage that predispose them to lead is the:
questions.explanation: The Great Man or Trait theory says leaders are born with qualities such as intelligence, charisma and courage, and that the fate of organisations depends on them. Option C looks at what leaders do rather than what they are, and A says the situation decides the right approach.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: A leadership theory that focuses on what leaders do, such as being task-oriented or people-oriented, rather than on what they are, is the:
questions.explanation: Behavioural theories focus on leaders' actions, for example whether they are task-oriented or people-oriented, as the key to leadership success. Options B and D focus on inborn qualities, the opposite emphasis.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Contingency or situational theories of leadership state that:

options.a: Rewards and punishments are the only way to motivate
options.c: Followers should never take part in decisions
options.d: The situation should determine the leadership approach

questions.explanation: Contingency or situational theories hold that the right leadership approach depends on the situation and on how leaders and group members interact. Option B is the trait view and A is the transactional view.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Leaders who inspire and motivate followers to achieve more than the expected result, as in charismatic leadership, follow the:
questions.explanation: Transformational or inspirational leaders inspire followers to perform beyond expectations, and charismatic leadership is an example. Option D relies on rewards and punishments for meeting set targets rather than on inspiration.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Participative or democratic leadership theories argue that:

options.a: Involving followers in decision making promotes consensus and commitment
options.b: Leaders should rely mainly on rewards and punishments
options.d: Leaders should focus only on tasks, never on people

questions.explanation: Participative or democratic theories hold that involving followers in decisions builds consensus and commitment. Option B describes transactional leadership and C describes the trait view.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: A sales manager in Kano pays a N50,000 bonus to every sales officer who meets the monthly target and issues a query to those who fall short. Which leadership theory does this reflect?
questions.explanation: Using rewards for meeting targets and punishments for missing them is transactional leadership. Option C inspires people to go beyond expectations, D focuses on supporting and developing followers, and B involves them in decisions.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Before changing the shift schedule, the plant manager of a Port Harcourt bottling company holds meetings in which workers discuss and vote on three proposed options. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: Letting workers discuss and vote on the options involves them in the decision, which is participative or democratic leadership and builds commitment. Option B relies on rewards and punishments, while D and A focus on the leader's inborn qualities.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: A leader who focuses on empowering and supporting group members, showing empathy, listening, and committing to their personal and professional development rather than exercising authority, practises:
questions.explanation: Servant leadership puts the growth and support of group members first, through empathy, listening and commitment to their development, rather than through use of authority. Options A and C rely on rewards or command rather than service to followers.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: A board member says: 'Great leaders are born, not made; you either have the charisma and courage or you do not.' This view reflects the:
questions.explanation: Believing that leadership comes from inborn traits such as charisma and courage is the Great Man or Trait view. Option D says the situation decides the approach, and C says leadership depends on what leaders do, which can be learned.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: A bank branch manager in Ibadan is directive during a cash-system failure but consults staff freely during normal periods, explaining that 'the right style depends on the circumstances'. Which theory best explains this approach?
questions.explanation: Changing leadership approach to fit the circumstances is the core idea of contingency or situational theory. Options B and D tie leadership to inborn qualities and A is about rewards and punishments, none of which explains a deliberate change of style.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Leadership ethics requires leaders to:

options.a: Guide people with honesty, fairness, respect and accountability, considering all stakeholders rather than profit alone
options.b: Keep all decisions secret from employees
options.c: Pursue profit alone whatever the effect on others

questions.explanation: Leadership ethics means guiding people with honesty, fairness, respect and accountability while considering the interests of all stakeholders, not only profit. Option C focuses on profit alone, and B and D breach transparency and fairness.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Responsible leadership pays attention to ethics, sustainability and accountability, and considers the interests of:

options.b: Employees, customers, shareholders and the wider society

questions.explanation: Responsible leadership weighs the interests of employees, customers, shareholders and the wider society, and such leaders promote organisational effectiveness. Options A, C and D each consider only one group.

questions.topic: Corporate Governance, Leadership and Management as a Profession
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the leadership theories that explain how and why people lead?
questions.explanation: Comparative advantage is a theory of international trade, not of leadership. The leadership theories include Great Man/Trait, behavioural, contingency, transformational, participative, transactional and servant leadership, so options C, B and D all belong.

questions.question: Aliko Dangote, founder of the Dangote Group, was born in 1957 in which Nigerian state?
questions.explanation: Aliko Dangote was born in Kano in 1957, and his business began as a trading company. Options A, B and C are linked to other leaders or businesses in this group, not to Dangote's birthplace.

questions.question: The Dangote Group began in 1977 as a:

options.a: Commercial bank licensed by the Central Bank
options.c: State-owned cement factory bought at privatisation
options.d: Small commodity-trading business started with a loan from a relative

questions.explanation: Dangote started in 1977 as a commodity trader, funded with a loan from an uncle, and only later moved into manufacturing. Options B and C reflect much later stages of the group's growth, and A was never how Dangote began.

questions.question: Aliko Dangote's move from importing cement and sugar to producing them in Nigeria is an example of which strategy?
questions.explanation: Import substitution means replacing imported goods with locally produced ones, which is what Dangote did in cement and sugar. Option D is selling off a business, as Femi Otedola did with Forte Oil, and B is licensing a brand to others.

questions.question: A stated purpose of the Dangote Refinery, commissioned in Lagos in 2023, is to:

options.a: Replace cement production in the Dangote Group
options.b: Export crude oil without refining it
options.c: Reduce Nigeria's dependence on imported fuel
options.d: Increase Nigeria's imports of refined petroleum

questions.explanation: The Dangote Refinery was established to refine petroleum in Nigeria and so reduce dependence on imported fuel, an extension of the import substitution idea. Option D is the opposite of its purpose, and B would leave the country still importing refined products.

questions.question: The Dangote Group built which of the following into Africa's largest producer in its industry?
questions.explanation: Dangote built Africa's largest cement production company, with major plants such as Obajana in Kogi State. Options A, C and D are industries not associated with Dangote's flagship business.

questions.question: Aliko Dangote earned his business studies degree from:
questions.explanation: Dangote studied business at Al-Azhar University in Cairo, Egypt. Option B is where Ibukun Awosika studied chemistry, and A is where Cosmas Maduka attended an executive programme.

questions.question: Ibukun Awosika is best known as the founder of:

options.a: The Chair Centre Group, a furniture manufacturing business

questions.explanation: Ibukun Awosika founded The Chair Centre Group, a furniture manufacturing business. Option C was founded by Cosmas Maduka, B by Tony Elumelu, and D by Femi Otedola.

questions.question: In 2015 Ibukun Awosika became the first woman to hold which position?

options.a: Director-General of the Nigerian Institute of Management
options.c: Chairman of First Bank of Nigeria
options.d: Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria

questions.explanation: Ibukun Awosika was appointed Chairman of First Bank of Nigeria in 2015, the first woman to chair the bank. Option B was held by Herbert Wigwe, and D and A are public offices she did not hold.

questions.question: A young Nigerian woman wants to build a manufacturing brand in a male-dominated industry while championing corporate governance and ethical leadership. Whose career is the closest model?
questions.explanation: Ibukun Awosika built a furniture manufacturing brand in a male-dominated industry and is a strong advocate of corporate governance, ethical leadership and women's entrepreneurship. Options A, C and D are noted for other things: performance management, high-risk innovation and energy-sector restructuring.

questions.question: Femi Otedola became chairman of African Petroleum in 2007 and in 2010 renamed it:
questions.explanation: Otedola gained control of African Petroleum in 2007 and the company was renamed Forte Oil Plc in 2010. Option C is the power company he later focused on, B is linked to Tony Elumelu, and A to Cosmas Maduka.

questions.question: In 2019 Femi Otedola sold his stake in Forte Oil and concentrated on electricity generation through Geregu Power. This decision is best described as:
questions.explanation: Otedola divested from fuel marketing (Forte Oil) and moved into power generation (Geregu Power), a strategic divestment. Option D describes Dangote's strategy, and B and C do not describe selling one business to focus on another.

questions.question: Geregu Power Plc, associated with Femi Otedola, operates in which sector?
questions.explanation: Geregu Power operates a power plant and is in electricity generation, which is why Otedola's impact is linked to generation capacity. Options D, B and C are the sectors of Coscharis, The Chair Centre and Access Bank respectively.

questions.question: Before African Petroleum, Femi Otedola set up Zenon Petroleum and Gas in 2003, a company mainly involved in:

options.d: Fuel marketing and distribution, especially diesel

questions.explanation: Zenon Petroleum and Gas, set up in 2003, marketed and distributed fuel and became a major player in Nigeria's diesel market. Options A, B and C are unrelated industries.

questions.question: Cosmas Maduka, founder of the Coscharis Group, learned business through:

options.b: A graduate trainee scheme at a bank
options.d: A family inheritance of a large factory

questions.explanation: Cosmas Maduka is a product of the Igbo apprenticeship system: he trained under a relative in the motor spare-parts trade before starting his own business with very little capital. Options B, C and D do not describe his humble start.

questions.question: Coscharis began in 1977 as a business dealing in:
questions.explanation: Coscharis started in automobile spare parts and expanded into vehicle distribution and assembly. Option D is Dangote's flagship product, C is linked to oil companies, and B is Ibukun Awosika's industry.

questions.question: The name 'Coscharis' was formed by combining:

options.a: The names of two Nigerian cities
options.b: The names of two foreign partner companies
options.d: The founder's first name and his wife's name

questions.explanation: Coscharis combines Cosmas, the founder's first name, with Charis from Charity, his wife's name. Options A, B and C are invented explanations.

questions.question: Cosmas Maduka's leadership style is commonly described as:
questions.explanation: Maduka's leadership is described as faith-driven and discipline-oriented, and his impact includes youth mentorship. Option A is associated with Jack Welch, D with Tony Elumelu, and C with Satya Nadella.

questions.question: In 2015 Coscharis Motors became the sole distributor in Nigeria of which car brand?
questions.explanation: Coscharis Motors became Nigeria's sole BMW distributor in 2015 and also set up a Ford Ranger assembly plant. Option D is linked to a Dangote-Stellantis assembly plan, and A is Elon Musk's company.

questions.question: A traditional, mentorship-based business incubation system in which a young person trains under a master trader and is then given settlement capital is the:
questions.explanation: Under the Igbo apprenticeship system (Igba Boi), an apprentice serves a master trader and is then 'settled' with capital to start his own business. Option A is a quality method, and B is Tony Elumelu's investment philosophy.

questions.question: Under the Igbo apprenticeship system, an apprentice typically trains under a master trader for about:
questions.explanation: An Igba Boi apprentice typically serves a master trader for about five to seven years before being settled with capital. Options B and D are too short for the full apprenticeship, and C is far longer than usual.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the Igbo apprenticeship system (Igba Boi)?

options.c: Agreements enforced mainly by written contracts filed in court
options.d: Post-training settlement capital for the apprentice

questions.explanation: Igba Boi agreements rest on trust and are enforced by the community, not by court-filed written contracts. Options A, B and D are all genuine features of the system.

questions.question: The philosophy that Africa's private sector can transform the continent through long-term investment that creates both economic prosperity and social wealth is called:
questions.explanation: Africapitalism, promoted by Tony Elumelu, holds that the African private sector can transform Africa through long-term investment that creates economic and social wealth. Option B is Indra Nooyi's PepsiCo strategy, and C is the broader idea associated with Paul Polman.

questions.question: In 2010 Tony Elumelu founded both Heirs Holdings and:
questions.explanation: In 2010 Elumelu founded Heirs Holdings, his family investment company, and the Tony Elumelu Foundation, which promotes African entrepreneurship. Options D, A and C are linked to Herbert Wigwe, Femi Otedola and Ibukun Awosika respectively.

questions.question: In 2015 Tony Elumelu committed US$100 million to an entrepreneurship programme intended to:

options.a: Build a cement plant in every African country
options.b: Buy a controlling stake in Microsoft
options.c: Train, fund and mentor 10,000 African entrepreneurs over 10 years

questions.explanation: The 2015 pledge of US$100 million aimed to create 10,000 African entrepreneurs over ten years through training, funding and mentoring. This is why his impact is described as entrepreneurship-driven economic empowerment; options A, B and D are not part of it.

questions.question: Standard Trust Bank, led by Tony Elumelu, merged with which bank in 2005?
questions.explanation: Standard Trust Bank merged with United Bank for Africa in 2005, and Elumelu became group managing director of the enlarged UBA. Option D later merged with Access Bank, and C is the bank Ibukun Awosika chaired.

questions.question: Herbert Wigwe and his partner Aigboje Aig-Imoukhuede acquired which bank in 2002 and grew it into a multinational institution?
questions.explanation: Wigwe and Aig-Imoukhuede acquired Access Bank in 2002, and Wigwe later became its CEO in 2014, expanding it into a multinational group. Option A is associated with Tony Elumelu, and B with Ibukun Awosika.

questions.question: Access Bank's merger with Diamond Bank, under Herbert Wigwe's leadership, made it Nigeria's largest bank. This illustrates Wigwe's contribution to:
questions.explanation: Merging with Diamond Bank expanded Access Bank's size and reach, which reflects Wigwe's focus on banking consolidation and corporate expansion. Options C and D describe Dangote and Musk, and B is a traditional business training system.

questions.question: Herbert Wigwe's investment in education includes founding Wigwe University in:
questions.explanation: Wigwe founded Wigwe University in his hometown of Isiokpo, Rivers State, reflecting his investment in education and leadership development. Options A, B and D are places linked to other leaders.

questions.question: Jack Welch served as Chairman and CEO of General Electric (GE) from:
questions.explanation: Jack Welch led GE as Chairman and CEO from 1981 to 2001. Option B is Indra Nooyi's tenure as PepsiCo CEO, and A is Paul Polman's tenure at Unilever.

questions.question: The quality-improvement programme that Jack Welch introduced at General Electric in the mid-1990s was:
questions.explanation: Welch adopted Motorola's Six Sigma quality programme at GE in 1995, alongside performance-based ranking. Option D is Nooyi's PepsiCo strategy, C is Polman's Unilever plan, and A is the culture Nadella promoted at Microsoft.

questions.question: Each year a company's chief executive rewards the top 20% of managers with bonuses and stock options and dismisses the bottom 10%. This system is most closely associated with:
questions.explanation: Rewarding the top 20% and removing the bottom 10% is Jack Welch's performance-based ranking system, often called the vitality curve or 'rank and yank'. Options B, C and D are known for growth mindset, Performance with Purpose and sustainability.

questions.question: Jack Welch insisted that every GE business should be:

options.a: Number one or number two in its industry
options.b: Run entirely by founders' family members
options.c: The lowest-priced firm in every market

questions.explanation: Welch required each GE business to be No. 1 or No. 2 in its industry, otherwise it would be fixed, sold or closed, which reflects his focus on efficiency and restructuring. Options B, C and D do not describe his policy.

questions.question: Indra Nooyi served as CEO of PepsiCo from:
questions.explanation: Indra Nooyi was CEO of PepsiCo from 2006 to 2018. Option C is Jack Welch's tenure at GE and A is Paul Polman's tenure at Unilever.

questions.question: Indra Nooyi's strategy of pursuing long-term growth at PepsiCo while having a positive impact on society and the environment was called:
questions.explanation: Performance with Purpose was Nooyi's strategy at PepsiCo, linking business growth to healthier products and environmental responsibility. Option B is Elumelu's philosophy, A is Welch's quality method, and C is the title of Nadella's book.

questions.question: PepsiCo under Indra Nooyi grouped its products into 'fun for you', 'better for you' and 'good for you' categories and grew the healthier ones. This reflects:

options.b: A shift toward healthier product diversification

questions.explanation: Classifying products from indulgent to healthy and expanding the healthier lines was Nooyi's shift toward healthier product diversification. Option A is Jack Welch's method, and D contradicts the fact that PepsiCo kept and reshaped its product range.

questions.question: Satya Nadella became CEO of Microsoft in February 2014, succeeding:
questions.explanation: Satya Nadella was announced as Microsoft's CEO in February 2014, succeeding Steve Ballmer. Option C co-founded Microsoft and was CEO before Ballmer, B led GE, and D succeeded Indra Nooyi at PepsiCo.

questions.question: A new CEO wants to change a rigid 'know-it-all' corporate culture into one where employees keep learning and experimenting. Which leader's approach is the best model?

options.a: Jack Welch's 'No. 1 or No. 2' rule at GE
options.b: Aliko Dangote's import substitution in cement
options.c: Satya Nadella's growth-mindset leadership at Microsoft
options.d: Femi Otedola's divestment from Forte Oil

questions.explanation: Nadella promoted empathetic, growth-mindset leadership and continual learning, which revitalised Microsoft's culture. Option A is a portfolio rule, and D and B are business strategies rather than culture change.

questions.question: Satya Nadella is credited with transforming Microsoft into a:
questions.explanation: Under Nadella, Microsoft was transformed into a cloud-first company, building on his earlier work leading the cloud and enterprise group and Azure. Options A, B and D describe the industries of other leaders.

questions.question: Elon Musk founded SpaceX in 2002 and became CEO of which electric-vehicle company in 2008?
questions.explanation: Musk founded SpaceX in 2002 and became CEO of Tesla in 2008, after joining it as an investor and chairman in 2004. His high-risk, innovation-driven style is linked to electric vehicles and private space travel; options C, A and D were led by Welch, Nooyi and Polman.

questions.question: Elon Musk's leadership style is best described as:

options.a: Cautious and focused on avoiding new technology
options.b: Based mainly on an apprenticeship system

questions.explanation: Musk's leadership is high-risk and innovation-driven, which accelerated electric vehicle adoption and technological disruption. Option C describes Cosmas Maduka, and A is the opposite of Musk's approach.

questions.question: As CEO of Unilever (2009 to 2019), Paul Polman launched the Unilever Sustainable Living Plan in 2010, which aimed among other things to:

options.b: Close all factories in developing countries
options.c: Halve the environmental footprint of Unilever's products
options.d: Double the company's use of plastic packaging

questions.explanation: The Unilever Sustainable Living Plan, launched in November 2010 under Polman, aimed to halve the environmental footprint of the company's products while growing the business. Options A, B and D contradict its sustainability goals.

questions.question: Arguing that quarterly targets push managers into short-term decisions that hurt the business, a CEO stops giving short-term earnings guidance to investors. Which leader is famous for doing this?
questions.explanation: Paul Polman discontinued short-term earnings guidance at Unilever to focus managers on long-term, responsible performance, part of his promotion of responsible capitalism. Option D is known for strict short-term performance ranking, and B and A are not known for this decision.

questions.question: PESTLE analysis is most useful during:
questions.explanation: PESTLE looks at Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Legal and Environmental factors outside the firm, so it is a tool for scanning the external environment. Options C, A and D are internal management tasks dealing with staff, stock and budgets.

questions.question: An economic recession reduces consumer demand primarily because of:
questions.explanation: In a recession, job losses and falling incomes leave households with less money to spend after taxes, so demand falls. Options B and A would generally support spending rather than reduce it.

questions.question: Inflation may benefit debtors because:

options.a: The real value of the money they owe declines

questions.explanation: With inflation, a fixed amount of debt is repaid with money that buys less than when it was borrowed, so the real burden of the debt falls. Option C is wrong because interest rates often rise during inflation, and option B is the reverse of what inflation usually does to a currency.

questions.question: Which of the following is part of internal environment analysis?

options.c: Evaluating the firm's strengths in a SWOT analysis

questions.explanation: Strengths and weaknesses in SWOT come from inside the firm, such as its skills, resources and reputation. Options D, B and A all concern the external environment.

questions.question: In a SWOT analysis, opportunities arise from the:
questions.explanation: Opportunities and threats are the external half of SWOT, coming from markets, technology, government policy and competitors. Options C and D are internal matters that would be analysed as strengths or weaknesses, as would option B.

questions.question: An organisation's corporate culture directly influences its:
questions.explanation: Corporate culture is the shared values and norms inside the organisation, and it shapes how people judge right and wrong at work. Options C, D and A are macroeconomic variables outside the firm's control.

questions.question: Strategic flexibility mainly enhances a firm's:

options.a: Ability to adapt to changes in its environment

questions.explanation: Strategic flexibility is a firm's capacity to shift resources and change course quickly when the environment changes, so it can absorb shocks and take up new opportunities. Option B is wrong because flexibility helps a firm stay in markets rather than leave them. Options C and D are threats, not benefits.

questions.question: Economic liberalisation tends to increase:
questions.explanation: Economic liberalisation removes government restrictions such as price controls, licensing limits and state monopolies, so more firms can enter markets and competition rises. Option A is the opposite, since liberalisation breaks up protected positions. Options C and D describe tighter control, which liberalisation moves away from.

questions.question: A sustainable competitive advantage arises from resources that are:

options.a: Valuable, rare and hard to imitate

questions.explanation: A firm keeps its advantage over rivals when its resources and capabilities are valuable, rare and difficult for others to copy or substitute. Options B and C describe resources any competitor can obtain, so they cannot set a firm apart for long. Option D is wrong because an advantage that lasts only briefly is not sustainable.

questions.question: Which of the following is the greatest cause of uncertainty for a business because it lies outside management's control?
questions.explanation: Political instability is part of the external (macro) environment, so management cannot control it, and it can suddenly change policies, security and demand. Options A, B and D are internal factors that management can plan for and influence directly.

questions.question: A PESTLE analysis is MOST useful for assessing:
questions.explanation: PESTLE stands for Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Legal and Environmental factors, which together make up the broad external (macro) environment of a business. Option A is internal analysis, as in the strengths part of SWOT, option B is competitor analysis in the immediate market, and option D is an HR appraisal matter.

questions.question: Which of the following is part of a firm's internal environment?
questions.explanation: The internal environment consists of factors within the organisation that management can largely control, such as its culture, staff, structure and resources. Options B, C and D come from outside the firm and belong to the external environment, which management cannot control.

questions.question: Customers, suppliers and competitors are part of a firm's:
questions.explanation: The micro or task environment consists of external groups that deal directly with the firm and affect it day to day, such as customers, suppliers and competitors. Option A covers broad forces like the economy, politics and technology that affect all firms. Option B is wrong because these groups are outside the firm, and option D is just one part of the macro environment.

questions.question: The business environment of an organisation is best defined as:

options.a: Only the physical building in which the business operates
options.b: Only the customers who buy the firm's products
options.c: All the internal and external factors and forces that affect its operations and performance
options.d: Only the laws made by government for businesses

questions.explanation: The business environment is the full set of internal and external factors and forces that influence how a business operates and performs. Options A, B and D each pick out one small part and treat it as the whole.

questions.question: The factors within an organisation, such as its employees, culture, owners, board and physical resources, make up its:
questions.explanation: The internal environment consists of factors inside the organisation, such as staff, culture, owners, the board and physical resources, which management can largely influence. Options B and D are names for the broad external forces, and A is one part of that external environment.

questions.question: Factors outside an organisation that affect it but over which it has little or no direct control make up its:
questions.explanation: The external environment covers forces outside the firm, such as customers, competitors, the economy and government, which the firm cannot directly control but must respond to. Options B, C and D are all inside the organisation.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT part of a firm's external environment?

options.d: The skills of the firm's own employees

questions.explanation: The skills of the firm's own employees are an internal resource. Suppliers, the exchange rate and competitors in options B, A and C all lie outside the firm and form part of its external environment.

questions.question: Compared with the external environment, the internal environment of a business is:

options.a: Made up only of government policies
options.b: The same for every business in the country
options.d: More within the control of the firm's management

questions.explanation: Internal factors such as staff, structure and culture can be shaped by management, while external factors can only be anticipated and responded to. Option C describes the external environment, and B is wrong because each firm's internal environment is unique.

questions.question: The forces close to a company that directly affect its ability to serve its customers, such as suppliers, customers, competitors and intermediaries, make up its:
questions.explanation: The micro or task environment contains the specific groups close to the firm, such as customers, suppliers, competitors and intermediaries, that directly affect its daily operations. Option C refers to broad societal forces such as PESTLE factors, and D is inside the firm.

questions.question: The broad external forces that affect all businesses in an economy, such as political, economic, social and technological conditions, make up the:
questions.explanation: The macro or general environment is made up of broad forces such as political, economic, social, technological, legal and environmental conditions that affect all firms. Option D is the narrower set of groups that deal directly with one firm, and C and B are inside the organisation.

questions.question: Which of the following is a MICRO environment factor for a Lagos restaurant?

options.a: The level of internet penetration in Nigeria
options.b: The farmers and traders who supply its foodstuffs

questions.explanation: The restaurant's suppliers deal with it directly and affect its daily operations, so they are part of its micro environment. Options A, C and D are broad national conditions in the macro environment.

questions.question: Which of the following is a MACRO environment factor for a Nigerian manufacturing firm?

options.a: A new competitor opening next door
options.b: A dispute with its main raw-material supplier
options.c: A rise in the national inflation rate
options.d: A complaint from one of its distributors

questions.explanation: The national inflation rate affects all firms in the economy and is a macro (economic) factor. Options A, B and D involve specific suppliers, competitors and distributors that deal directly with the firm, so they are micro factors.

questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes the micro environment from the macro environment?

options.a: The micro environment affects a particular firm directly, while the macro environment consists of broad forces affecting all firms
options.b: The micro environment is inside the firm, while the macro environment is outside it
options.c: The micro environment includes only government, while the macro environment includes only customers
options.d: There is no real difference; they are two names for the same thing

questions.explanation: Both are external, but the micro environment consists of groups that deal with a particular firm directly, while the macro environment is the broad set of forces affecting every firm. Option B confuses micro with internal, a common mix-up.

questions.question: In PESTLE analysis, the letters stand for:

options.a: Product, Economic, Sales, Technology, Labour and Employment
options.b: Political, Ethical, Strategic, Tactical, Legal and Economic
options.c: Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Legal and Environmental
options.d: Planning, Economic, Strategic, Technical, Leadership and Ethical

questions.explanation: PESTLE stands for Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Legal and Environmental factors in the macro environment. Options A, B and D mix in words that are not part of the framework.

questions.question: Which environment does a PESTLE analysis NOT directly examine?

options.a: The economic conditions facing all firms
options.b: The legal framework businesses must obey
options.c: The political climate of the country
options.d: The firm's internal strengths and weaknesses

questions.explanation: PESTLE scans the external macro environment, so it does not directly examine a firm's internal strengths and weaknesses, which are assessed through tools such as the strengths and weaknesses part of SWOT. Options A, B and C are exactly what PESTLE covers.

questions.question: Ahead of a general election, investors delay projects in Nigeria because they are unsure whether a new government will continue existing economic policies. Under PESTLE, this uncertainty is mainly a(n):
questions.explanation: Uncertainty about elections, government stability and the direction of government policy is a political factor. Option A concerns innovation, D concerns the natural environment, and C concerns demographics and culture.

questions.question: A Nigerian importer finds that the naira price of a container of goods has risen from N18 million to N27 million because the naira has weakened against the dollar. Under PESTLE, this is a(n):
questions.explanation: Exchange rate movements are an economic factor, because they change the cost of imports and the purchasing power of money. Option C would require a change in the law, and D and A concern society and technology.

questions.question: Rising inflation means a family in Ibadan can now buy less food with the same N50,000 monthly budget, so a supermarket's sales volume falls. Under PESTLE, the supermarket is affected by a(n):
questions.explanation: Inflation reduces real purchasing power, which is an economic factor in the macro environment. Option D relates to government stability and policy direction, C to the natural environment, and B to laws.

questions.question: The Central Bank of Nigeria raises its monetary policy rate, and a manufacturer's bank loan becomes more expensive. Under PESTLE, the higher cost of borrowing is best classified as a(n):
questions.explanation: Interest rates and the cost of credit are economic factors, because they affect how expensive it is for firms to borrow and invest. Options B, C and D concern society, innovation and the natural environment.

questions.question: A Nigerian company notices that a large and growing share of the population is young and moving into cities, so it launches products aimed at young urban buyers. Under PESTLE, it is responding to a(n):
questions.explanation: Population structure, age distribution and urbanisation are social (socio-cultural) factors. Option A would involve a new law, C would involve government or elections, and B the natural environment.

questions.question: A food company in Kano reformulates its products and adjusts its advertising to respect the religious and cultural values of its customers. Under PESTLE, it is responding to a(n):
questions.explanation: Religion, culture, values and lifestyles are social factors that shape what customers will buy and how they respond to marketing. Option C concerns prices and incomes, A innovation, and D the natural environment.

questions.question: The rapid spread of smartphones and mobile payment apps in Nigeria allows a small Aba shoe-maker to sell online and receive payments instantly. Under PESTLE, this is a(n):
questions.explanation: New tools such as smartphones, the internet and mobile payments are technological factors that create new ways of doing business. Options B, C and D concern government, laws and the natural environment.

questions.question: A bank in Lagos replaces many manual teller transactions with automated machines and online banking. The development that made this possible is mainly a(n):
questions.explanation: Automation and online banking are technological developments that change how services are produced and delivered. Option C could influence how quickly customers adopt it, but the change itself comes from technology.

questions.question: After the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 was signed into law, a fintech company had to change how it collects and stores customers' personal information. Under PESTLE, this is a(n):
questions.explanation: A law that sets rules businesses must obey, such as the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023, is a legal factor. Options A, C and D do not involve binding legal rules.

questions.question: A new labour law raises the minimum wage that employers must pay, and a Nigerian factory must increase its wage bill. Under PESTLE, the requirement to pay the new wage is best classified as a(n):
questions.explanation: A statutory requirement that employers must obey, such as a minimum wage law, is a legal factor. Options B, C and D do not create binding obligations of this kind.

questions.question: In PESTLE analysis, the difference between political and legal factors is that:

options.a: Political factors concern government stability, ideology and policy direction, while legal factors concern the actual laws and regulations businesses must obey
options.b: Political factors are internal, while legal factors are external
options.c: There is no difference; the two terms are interchangeable
options.d: Political factors concern only taxes, while legal factors concern only elections

questions.explanation: Political factors relate to the stability, attitudes and direction of government, while legal factors are the specific laws and regulations that bind businesses. Option D swaps and narrows the ideas, and B is wrong because both are external.

questions.question: Heavy seasonal flooding damages a warehouse in Kogi State and cuts road access for weeks. Under PESTLE, this is a(n):
questions.explanation: Weather, climate and natural events such as floods are environmental (ecological) factors. Options A, C and D concern society, laws and technology rather than the natural environment.

questions.question: Communities in an oil-producing area complain about pollution from a company's operations, and the company invests in cleaner production and waste control. Under PESTLE, the pollution issue is mainly a(n):
questions.explanation: Pollution, waste and the impact of operations on the natural environment are environmental factors. Option A may be part of the solution, but the issue being responded to is environmental.

questions.question: The main purpose of carrying out a PESTLE analysis is to:

options.a: Decide the salaries of individual employees
options.b: Record the daily sales of each product
options.c: Identify external macro-environmental factors that may create opportunities or threats
options.d: Calculate the firm's net profit for the year

questions.explanation: PESTLE helps managers scan the macro environment to spot political, economic, social, technological, legal and environmental changes that may become opportunities or threats. Options A, B and D are accounting or HR tasks, not environmental analysis.

questions.question: The process of monitoring and analysing the external environment to detect changes that may affect a business is called:
questions.explanation: Environmental scanning means systematically watching the external environment for trends and changes that may affect the firm, and PESTLE is one tool for doing it. Options B, C and D are HR, marketing and finance techniques.

questions.question: In SWOT analysis, which elements come from the internal environment?
questions.explanation: Strengths and weaknesses are internal features of the firm, while opportunities and threats come from the external environment. Option B is the external half, and C and A mix internal and external elements.

questions.question: A Nigerian paint manufacturer finds that its machines are old and its staff lack modern skills. In SWOT terms, these are:

options.a: Threats arising from the external environment
options.b: Strengths arising from the micro environment
options.c: Weaknesses arising from the internal environment
options.d: Opportunities arising from the macro environment

questions.explanation: Old machines and skill gaps are internal shortcomings, so they are weaknesses. Option A wrongly places them outside the firm, and D and B misdescribe them as favourable.

questions.question: A foreign company with lower prices opens a large plant in Nigeria and begins taking customers from a local biscuit maker. For the local firm, this is best described as:

options.a: A strength in its internal environment
options.b: An opportunity in its internal environment
options.c: A weakness in its internal environment
options.d: A threat in its micro (task) environment

questions.explanation: A new competitor is an external group that directly affects the firm, so it is part of the micro environment and, here, a threat. Options A, B and C wrongly treat an outside competitor as an internal factor.

questions.question: A Nigerian bottling company loses sales after its biggest distributor in the South-West goes out of business. The distributor is part of the company's:
questions.explanation: Distributors are marketing intermediaries who deal with the company directly, so they belong to its micro (task) environment. Option D refers to broad national forces, and C is inside the company.

questions.question: Which of the following groups is part of a firm's micro environment?
questions.explanation: Customers interact directly with the firm and determine its sales, so they are part of the micro environment. Options A, B and C are broad macro forces affecting all firms.

questions.question: A company's board of directors and its owners (shareholders) are best classified as part of its:
questions.explanation: Owners and the board of directors are inside the organisation's structure of control, so they are part of the internal environment. Options A, C and D are external.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an economic factor in the macro environment?
questions.explanation: Religious beliefs are a social factor, not an economic one. Inflation, exchange rates and interest rates in options A, C and D are standard economic factors.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a social factor in PESTLE analysis?

options.b: A new tax law passed by the National Assembly

questions.explanation: A new tax law is a legal factor, because it is a binding rule businesses must obey. Population, education and culture in options D, A and C are social factors.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a technological factor?
questions.explanation: A fall in household incomes is an economic factor. Internet access, automation and mobile payments in options B, D and A are technological factors.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an environmental (ecological) factor?
questions.explanation: Climate change and extreme weather are environmental factors in PESTLE. Option B is political, A belongs to the micro environment, and C is internal.

questions.question: The Federal Government reduces import duty on industrial machinery, and a Nigerian packaging firm saves N3 million on a new production line. This shows that changes in the external environment can:

options.a: Create opportunities as well as threats for businesses
options.b: Be controlled directly by the firm's managers
options.c: Affect only the firm's internal culture

questions.explanation: External changes are not always harmful; a lower import duty cuts costs and opens an opportunity to expand. Option D ignores favourable changes, B wrongly suggests firms control government policy, and C misplaces an external change inside the firm.

questions.question: An environment in which conditions change rapidly and unpredictably is described as:
questions.explanation: A dynamic environment is one where conditions such as prices, technology and regulations change often and unpredictably, which increases uncertainty for managers. Options A and B describe environments where conditions change little.

questions.question: A Nigerian firm's managers cannot stop a rise in global crude oil prices, but they can adjust their pricing and sourcing in response. This illustrates that external environmental factors are:

options.a: Irrelevant to firms that do not sell oil
options.b: Largely uncontrollable, so managers must anticipate and adapt to them
options.c: Part of the firm's internal environment

questions.explanation: External factors such as world oil prices are outside the firm's control, so managers anticipate them and adapt their strategies. Option D is wrong because no firm can set world prices, and C misplaces the factor inside the firm.

questions.question: A Nigerian fashion brand notices that more young customers now prefer locally made clothing and promote it on social media. To the brand, this change in taste is mainly:

options.a: A political factor that creates a threat
options.b: A social factor that creates an opportunity
options.d: A legal factor that creates a threat

questions.explanation: A shift in tastes and lifestyles is a social factor, and because it favours the brand's products it is an opportunity. Options A and D misclassify it, and C wrongly places it inside the firm.

questions.question: Which of the following is part of a firm's internal environment?

options.a: The level of insecurity in the country

questions.explanation: A firm's money, machinery and other physical resources belong to its internal environment. Options A, B and D are external conditions that the firm cannot directly control.

questions.question: A Nigerian state government announces a new policy direction that favours locally produced goods in all public procurement. For local manufacturers, this is mainly a:

options.a: Social factor that creates a weakness
options.b: Technological factor that creates a threat
options.c: Political factor that creates an opportunity
options.d: Internal factor that creates a strength

questions.explanation: A government's policy direction and priorities are political factors, and a policy that favours local goods is an opportunity for local manufacturers. Option A confuses an external factor with an internal weakness, and D wrongly places it inside the firm.

questions.question: Rising insecurity on highways makes it risky for a Kaduna food distributor to move goods, increasing its insurance and security costs. This shows how the external environment can:

options.b: Be changed directly by one firm's managers
options.c: Increase operating costs and reduce performance

questions.explanation: Insecurity is an external condition that raises costs for security, insurance and logistics and so harms performance. Options A and B wrongly suggest that external factors can be ignored or controlled by one firm.

questions.question: Why should managers study the business environment?

options.a: To anticipate changes, seize opportunities and reduce the impact of threats
options.d: To avoid the need for planning

questions.explanation: Studying the environment helps managers foresee changes, take advantage of opportunities and prepare for threats, which supports better planning. Option C is false because environments change constantly, and D is the opposite of the purpose.

questions.question: A small business in Enugu earns N2 million in monthly sales. Its owner says: 'Inflation, interest rates and government policies are not my concern; only my shop matters.' The best response is that:

options.a: Macro factors affect only government agencies
options.b: The owner is right, because macro factors affect only large firms
options.c: The owner is right, because small firms have no external environment
options.d: Macro factors affect all businesses, including small ones, through costs, prices and demand

questions.explanation: Macro forces such as inflation, interest rates and government policy affect every business, small or large, through the prices it pays, the prices it can charge and customer demand. Options A, B and C wrongly limit the reach of the macro environment.

questions.question: A Nigerian telecom company sees two developments: (1) a new regulation requires all SIM cards to be linked to national identification numbers, and (2) mobile internet use is growing rapidly. Which PESTLE classification is correct?
questions.explanation: A binding regulation on SIM registration is a legal factor, while the spread of mobile internet is a technological factor. Option C reverses the two, a common error, and A and B misclassify both.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly lists two components of the micro (task) environment?
questions.explanation: Suppliers and competitors deal directly with the firm and form part of its micro environment. Options A, B and D are pairs of macro factors (economic, environmental and political).

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT part of a firm's micro (task) environment?
questions.explanation: National fiscal policy is a broad political-economic force that affects all firms, so it belongs to the macro environment. Customers, suppliers and competitors in options C, D and B deal directly with the firm and form its micro environment.

questions.topic: Functional Areas I: Marketing and Human Resources
questions.question: Market segmentation improves a firm's marketing strategy mainly by:
questions.explanation: Segmentation splits a broad market into groups with similar needs, so the firm can choose and serve the most attractive groups with tailored offers. Options C, A and B are finance and governance matters that have nothing to do with how a market is divided.

questions.topic: Functional Areas I: Marketing and Human Resources
questions.question: In marketing, positioning refers to:

options.a: The image of a brand in customers' minds relative to competitors

questions.explanation: Positioning is the final step of STP: creating a distinct, desirable image for the product in the target customers' minds so it stands out from rivals. Option D sounds similar but is about where goods sit in a shop, and option B belongs to the place element of the marketing mix.

questions.topic: Functional Areas I: Marketing and Human Resources
questions.question: Workforce (human resource) planning mainly ensures that:

options.d: The organisation has the right number of people with the right skills when needed

questions.explanation: Workforce planning forecasts future staffing needs and compares them with current staff so gaps in numbers and skills can be filled through recruitment or training. Options A, C and B are finance, tax and governance concerns rather than people planning.

questions.topic: Functional Areas I: Marketing and Human Resources
questions.question: The effectiveness of a training programme is best measured using:

options.b: Changes in trainees' behaviour and job performance

questions.explanation: Training is effective when trainees apply what they learnt, so the best evidence is improved behaviour and performance on the job. Options A, D and C reflect the whole firm's finances or market position and are affected by many things besides training.

questions.topic: Functional Areas I: Marketing and Human Resources
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the 4Ps of the marketing mix?
questions.explanation: The 4Ps are product, price, place and promotion. People is added only in the extended services marketing mix (the 7Ps), so it is not one of the original four; options D, C and A are all part of the 4Ps.

questions.topic: Functional Areas I: Marketing and Human Resources
questions.question: High employee engagement mainly improves:
questions.explanation: Engaged employees are committed and put in discretionary effort, which raises output and service quality. Options D, B and C are economic or financial measures that employee attitudes do not directly control.

questions.topic: Functional Areas I: Marketing and Human Resources
questions.question: High employee turnover increases:
questions.explanation: When employees leave frequently, the firm must keep advertising, selecting and training replacements, so recruitment and training costs rise. Option A is wrong because these extra costs drain cash rather than add to it. Options B and C are unrelated to staff leaving.

questions.topic: Functional Areas I: Marketing and Human Resources
questions.question: A market penetration strategy aims at:

options.a: Growing sales of existing products in existing markets

questions.explanation: Market penetration means selling more of the products a firm already has to the customers and markets it already serves, for example through lower prices or heavier promotion. Option B describes market development, and option C describes diversification, which involves new products and new markets. Option D is cutting back operations, the opposite of a growth strategy.

questions.topic: Functional Areas I: Marketing and Human Resources
questions.question: Giving teams more autonomy is most likely to improve:
questions.explanation: Autonomy means letting team members decide how to do their work, and having that control and responsibility tends to raise motivation and commitment. Options B, C and D are economy-wide conditions that a firm's team design cannot change.

questions.topic: Functional Areas I: Marketing and Human Resources
questions.question: Succession planning reduces the risk of:
questions.explanation: Succession planning identifies and develops people who can step into important positions, so when a leader leaves or retires there is someone ready to take over. Options A and C are economy-wide conditions, and option D is a financing matter that grooming future leaders does not address.

questions.topic: Functional Areas I: Marketing and Human Resources
questions.question: Which decision BEST demonstrates the marketing concept?

options.a: Producing at the lowest possible cost
options.c: Starting production only after market research

questions.explanation: The marketing concept says a firm should first find out what customers need and want, then produce to satisfy those needs better than competitors. Option A reflects the production concept, and option B reflects the selling concept, which pushes whatever has been made. Option D is a cost decision, not a customer-focused philosophy.

questions.topic: Functional Areas I: Marketing and Human Resources
questions.question: Which HR activity MOST directly supports change management?
questions.explanation: Change usually requires people to learn new skills, systems and ways of working, and training and development is the HR activity that equips them to do so. Options A and D are routine pay matters, and option B brings in new people but does nothing for the existing staff who must adapt.

questions.topic: Functional Areas I: Marketing and Human Resources
questions.question: Which marketing approach generally suits Nigeria's rural consumer markets best?

options.a: Premium pricing based on brand prestige
options.d: Stressing global fashion trends and luxury aesthetics

questions.explanation: Rural Nigerian consumers often have lower incomes, are careful about quality and value, and prefer products that are functional and long-lasting, so value-for-money offers suit them. Options A and D fit higher-income urban buyers who respond to brand image and international trends. Option C is wrong because, although mobile access is growing in rural areas, open markets and kiosks still matter a great deal there.

questions.topic: Functional Areas I: Marketing and Human Resources
questions.question: Urban consumers in Nigeria are more likely to switch brands mainly because of their:
questions.explanation: City consumers see many competing brands in modern retail outlets and through digital and international marketing, so they have more choice and information and switch more easily. Options A, B and D would make switching less likely, not more, and they do not describe typical urban buyers.

questions.topic: Functional Areas I: Marketing and Human Resources
questions.question: In modern marketing, the term 'market' is best described as:

options.a: Only the physical location where buyers and sellers meet to trade
options.b: All individuals and organisations that are actual or potential buyers of a product
options.c: The total stock of goods a firm has available for sale
options.d: The group of firms that produce and sell the same product

questions.explanation: Because of innovation and globalisation, a market now means the actual or potential buyers of a product, not just a place. Option A is the older, narrower meaning of a market as a location. Option D describes an industry (the sellers), while Option C describes inventory.

questions.topic: Functional Areas I: Marketing and Human Resources
questions.question: A marketing manager says 'the car market in Nigeria is growing.' In the modern sense of the word, she is referring to:

options.a: Only people who bought a car in the last twelve months
options.b: The factories that assemble cars within Nigeria
options.c: The car dealership lots located along major Lagos roads
options.d: All individuals and organisations that are actual or potential buyers of cars

questions.explanation: A car market refers to all individuals and organisations that are actual or potential buyers of cars, not a particular place where cars are sold. Option C treats the market as a location, and Option A leaves out potential buyers. Option B describes producers, not buyers.

questions.topic: Functional Areas I: Marketing and Human Resources
questions.question: The market made up of all individuals who purchase goods and services for direct consumption or household use is the:
questions.explanation: The consumer market consists of individuals buying for their own direct consumption or household use. Option B, the industrial market, buys goods for further production. Options A and C are not the category being described here.

questions.topic: Functional Areas I: Marketing and Human Resources
questions.question: A construction company in Abuja buys 2,000 bags of cement to use in building an estate. In this purchase, the company is part of the:
questions.explanation: The industrial market includes organisations, such as construction firms, that buy goods and services for further production. Option B is wrong because the cement is not bought for direct household consumption. Options A and D also describe buying for final or household use.

questions.topic: Functional Areas I: Marketing and Human Resources
questions.question: Which of the following purchases does NOT belong to the industrial market?

options.a: A family buying rice and vegetables for its own meals
options.b: A mining firm buying explosives for its quarry operations
options.c: A transport company buying tyres for its fleet of buses
options.d: A fishery buying nets to expand its catch

questions.explanation: Industrial buyers purchase goods for further production, while a family buying food for its own meals is a consumer purchase. Options B, C and D are organisations in transport, mining and fisheries buying inputs for their operations, which places them in the industrial market.

questions.topic: Functional Areas I: Marketing and Human Resources
questions.question: The starting point of marketing activities is:

options.a: Delivering finished goods to retail outlets
options.b: Collecting payment from customers after a sale
options.c: Setting the advertising budget for the year
